articles.title: Antonelli quiere 'destrozar' a Vettel
articles.standfirst: El piloto italiano viene de coronarse como el campeón más joven en la historia de la F1
articles.summary: El piloto italiano viene de coronarse como el campeón más joven en la historia de la F1
articles.body: El nombre de Kimi Antonelli quedará grabado para siempre en los libros de historia de la Fórmula 1... al menos hasta que alguien se atreva a destronarlo. La semana pasada, con su tercer puesto en el Gran Premio de México, el piloto italiano se convirtió en el campeón del mundo más joven de todos los tiempos. Un hito que confirma el impacto de un talento llamado a marcar una época en la categoría reina del automovilismo. Con apenas 20 años, Antonelli ha dejado atrás el récord que Sebastian Vettel estableció en 2010. Sin embargo, el italiano no parece conformarse con haber superado al alemán en precocidad. Todavía tiene varios desafíos por delante y quiere aprovechar las últimas carreras del calendario para seguir 'destrozando' sus registros. La temporada entra en su recta final y, con el título ya en el bolsillo, el joven piloto tiene margen para competir sin la presión de jugarse el campeonato. Con cuatro grandes premios todavía por disputarse, hay una marca que ya resulta inalcanzable: las 19 victorias que Max Verstappen consiguió en 2023. Sin embargo, Antonelli sí podría igualar las 13 que Sebastian Vettel firmó en 2013 y Michael Schumacher en 2004, dos de las temporadas más dominantes que se recuerdan. Para lograrlo, tendría que ganar las cuatro carreras que restan. La primera oportunidad llegará este mismo fin de semana, en el Gran Premio de Brasil, donde el italiano ya terminó segundo la pasada temporada. Tonybet sitúa a Antonelli entre los principales candidatos a llevarse la victoria... aunque no parte como favorito. Su triunfo cotiza a 3.24, por detrás de Max Verstappen, que aparece en cabeza con una cuota de 2.24. Las apuestas deportivas anticipan un nuevo pulso entre ambos, en un circuito que puede ofrecer al italiano la primera oportunidad de acercarse a ese récord de 13 victorias. Si consigue imponerse en Brasil, además, duplicará los cinco triunfos que Vettel logró en 2010, el año en el que conquistó su primer Mundial. Antonelli ya tiene el trabajo hecho y nadie podrá arrebatarle el honor de ser el campeón más joven de la historia de la Fórmula 1. Pero estas últimas cuatro carreras servirán para medir hasta dónde llega su ambición. Las mejores casas de apuestas seguirán de cerca su rendimiento en Brasil y en los siguientes grandes premios, mientras el italiano busca convertir un año histórico en una temporada todavía más memorable. El primer asalto a los récords de Vettel empieza en Interlagos. articles.title: Ohio State Captain Says It's 'Playoff Time Now' For No. 11 Buckeyes
articles.summary: Ohio State football is focusing on mental preparation this week after dropping from No. 2 to No. 11 in the Associated Press poll.
articles.body: In between playing two of the more physically gifted teams on the schedule, Ohio State football’s focus this week is more on the mental side of things. The Buckeyes (6-2, 4-1 Big Ten, No. 12 CFP) dropped from No. 2 in the Associated Press poll last week to No. 11 following a 30-18 loss at USC. The timing of their second setback of the season could have been better as the College Football Playoff committee released its first rankings Tuesday night. The Buckeyes came in at 12th — effectively out of the field if the playoff started this week because a team from a Group of 5 conference will get an automatic bid. "It’s pretty much playoff time now for us cuz we can’t lose," junior linebacker Payton Pierce said. "And so there’s a sense of urgency, and intensity, and focus." Pierce is a captain, so he is part of the chain of command when it comes to leadership, but he said it starts at the top with head coach Ryan Day. What is Day’s message? "We gotta go — leave it all on the field," Pierce said. "There’s no stepping back, no regrets. Guys gotta go out there and let it rip." More than one player expressed some concern that effort was lacking at times in the loss to the Trojans, who were facing their own CFP mortality after getting throttled at Wisconsin on Oct. 24 to fall to 6-2. Safety Jaylen McClain was the first to mention effort during postgame interviews in Los Angeles, and linebacker Christian Alliegro confirmed they saw issues during film review Sunday. This week it sounds like Day is on the warpath to prevent a repeat — not only out of a sense of pride but also a feeling the Buckeyes (6-2) might be out of chances to make the postseason if they stumble this week against Oregon (5-3, 3-2 Big Ten) or in subsequent games against Northwestern, Nebraska and Michigan. "The playoffs have started early for us," running back Isaiah West said. "If we win, we continue. If we lose, we put ourselves in a really bad spot, so the sense of urgency is at an all-time high." West described the feelings around the building as "heavy," but he also said multiple times, "We’ll be just fine." It’s a delicate balance between being locked in and playing too tight. Although Day’s teams have rarely lost a game — let alone two — prior to the last week of the season during his eight years at the helm in Columbus, he has had to navigate them through tough times before. Most notably was two years ago when the Buckeyes were reeling after a 13-10 loss to Michigan in which they might have been too amped to play their best. After three weeks of soul searching, they looked rejuvenated in a throttling of Tennessee to kick off a four-game run to the CFP National Championship. "He’s had a great message this week, and we know what’s at stake so we’re just taking it one day at a time right now," Pierce said. This week they play host to an Oregon team that's already lost three games despite boasting a star-studded roster that had the Ducks ranked No. 2 behind Ohio State to start the season. They showed resiliency last week by rallying to beat Northwestern, an effort that has them No. 23 in the CFP rankings this week but just outside the AP Top 25. "As we go through the season, we’re growing, we’re building," Day said. "We’re building some momentum, and then we had this game at USC. If we don’t learn our lesson from this game right here, there’s gonna be a lot of regret in that locker room. So the urgency has gotta be as high as it’s ever been, and everybody has to understand what’s at stake here moving forward. "And it’s the coach’s job to make sure they understand that, and it’s the leaders’ job who’ve been around here before, that have played here before, that know what it’s like to make sure that they’re relaying that message as well." articles.title: 2027 Gold Cup Format Changes Will See USA, Mexico Part Of Two Groups Of 8 Teams
articles.summary: CONCACAF has announced a new format for the Gold Cup soccer tournament, shifting from four groups to two starting with the next edition.
articles.body: The Gold Cup soccer tournament – which features squads like the U.S. men's national team and Mexico's men's national team – will shift from a four-group format of 16 teams to a two-group structure starting with its next edition, the North American governing body known as CONCACAF said Thursday. Through last year's tournament, the Gold Cup featured 16 national teams divided into four groups of four, with the top two teams from each group advancing to the quarterfinals. Under the new format, the two groups will consist of eight countries each, with the top four teams from each advancing. The new structure guarantees all participating teams at least four matches instead of three. "We are really excited about what this new format will bring to the tournament’s group stage," CONCACAF president Victor Montagliani said. "Every match will matter, with teams facing a balanced mix of opponents and competing for a place in the knockout rounds." The 2027 tournament, which is expected to have at least some games in the United States, will kick off on June 17 and conclude with the final on July 11. The draw will take place on April 8. The next Gold Cup will feature 15 countries from the region qualifying through the Nations League, alongside guest nation Saudi Arabia. The 2025 edition saw Mexico beat the USMNT, 2-1, in Houston. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Goalscorers Have Personality And A Big Ego. Ronaldo Was The Best At All That.
articles.summary: Elite goalscorers, by nature, have to be selfish. Which is why Cristiano Ronaldo excelled at being both.
articles.body: By the time Cristiano Ronaldo was 12 years old, the decision had been made for him to leave his home on the island of Madeira and move to the Portuguese capital of Lisbon. Here was a boy, who shared a bedroom with his three siblings, the son of a hospitality cleaner and a father who was a war veteran and struggled with alcoholism, ready to take his first main step into the unknown. There were obstacles when he arrived at Sporting CP's youth academy. Plenty of them. Ronaldo, in fact, struggled with school so much that he was once expelled for throwing a chair at a teacher. He eventually persuaded his mother on the unthinkable – that education was not a priority and, essentially, he pleaded with her and his Sporting tutor to allow him to quit and focus on football alone. It was obviously a gamble. He has even said it before. Had he not become a professional footballer, due to leaving school so early, Ronaldo had probably envisioned a life as a local fisherman. Then there was the heart problem. At 15, he was diagnosed with tachycardia – a condition that caused an abnormally fast heart rate – even whilst he rested. This prompted surgery and was a terrifying situation for a young kid to deal with. But the surgery was successful and from that moment on, Cristiano Ronaldo’s full story began. Here’s the other fact that most people forget. Ronaldo is not his last name. It’s Dos Santos Aveiro. I presume it’s only right for Cristiano to have the name as Ronaldo, because like Reagan, he is known for being deeply disciplined with a slightly detached strategy against opponents. Like Reagan, a former actor, Ronaldo has also never been one to shy away from the limelight. And that’s essentially what turned him into the player he ultimately became. There is a perfection to Ronaldo’s football that is both inspiring and overwhelming. His search for an omnipotent identity has always been his greatest strength and, at times, his Achilles heel. Whilst Lionel Messi’s diminutive stature and introspective personality captivated fans from one dimension, Ronaldo's focus was a flawless pursuit of impeccable athleticism and force. His training regime and eating habits are ludicrous to you or me, but it’s his obsession with discipline that gave him this 23-year career on the international stage. With regard to his actual game, I have always said that Ronaldo, to me, is the greatest goalscorer and finisher the men’s game will ever witness. And this, my friends, is the hardest job in football. To score goals. His 146 goals for Portugal, each one of them, were gigantic statements. Even the penalties. It’s why he celebrates with "SIUUUU" – an exaggerated expression of "si" — the Spanish and Portuguese word for yes. The celebration is an acceptance of grandiosity. A door of pomposity where the stadium, in unison, coronates him after landing on the ground after the 180 degree jump. The entire notion of the celebration, now glorified and globalized around the world, is Ronaldo’s way of telling the opponent, the stadium, the world, that – at this very moment – he is the one in charge. The longevity of his career is also something to truly respect and appreciate. When he played his first European Championship, Lamine Yamal was three. Ronaldo is the only player to have featured at six Euros. It’s almost inconceivable to believe that the one he led Portugal as champion (after a 1-0 win over then-host France) came in 2016. Alongside Messi and Guillermo "Memo" Ochoa, he has also appeared in six World Cup editions (though Messi and Ronaldo were the ones to play in each one). Across the two marquee competitions (Euros and World Cup), Ronaldo also scored 25 goals. No other player has that record. Since 2004, Ronaldo has scored at least one goal for Portugal for 23 straight calendar years. He also holds the record for most men’s international appearances with 234 and his quest to score 1,000 goals will continue during his time with his club Al-Nassr. These are incredible numbers. The five-time Ballon d’Or winner will retire from Portugal, however, without a World Cup. And this will undoubtedly remain a ghost that he will never be able to scare away. His recent altercation with national team manager Jorge Jesus after leaving camp in the previous window, followed by a lengthy statement on social media, was the reluctance of a once-complete specimen admitting that his powers are dwindling. He just didn’t want to come to terms with it. In the same way Narcissus died because of being too enamored with his own reflection, I think Ronaldo’s supercilious personality often became his own worst enemy. articles.title: Who Are Tom Brady's Top 4 NFL MVP Candidates? The GOAT Assesses The Favorites
articles.summary: Tom Brady shared four players he believes are vying for the NFL MVP award.
articles.body: Tom Brady earned three NFL Most Valuable Player awards with the New England Patriots. That gives him more than enough credence to assess the candidates for that award now that he's retired from the league and is an NFL broadcaster. So when posed with the question on FOX Sports' "Ask Tom," Brady shared a few candidates for the 2026 MVP. Most of Brady's candidates aren't surprises. However, he's throwing a running back into the MVP race through the first half of the season, as a non-quarterback hasn't won the award since 2012. Here are Brady's top four MVP candidates, and their odds to win the award, according to FanDuel. Josh Allen, QBBuffalo Bills Brady: "Josh Allen is playing great football. And that quarterback position we know impacts Josh is throwing it in, running it in. He's doing a great job." Stats: 1,793 passing yards, 11 touchdown passes, five interceptions, 101.1 passer rating; 270 rushing yards, nine touchdown runs (through seven games). Odds: At +165, Allen is the clear MVP favorite. So, it's no surprise Brady listed him first. Brock Purdy, QBSan Francisco 49ers Brady: "The 6-1 49ers — I don't think they would be in that position without Brock's steady, dependable, consistent play. He's done so many great things." Stats: 1,748 passing yards, 15 touchdowns, four interceptions and a 110.1 passer rating (through seven games). Odds: Purdy is third on the odds board at +500, proving his week-in, week-out leadership in San Francisco is being recognized by more than just Brady. Jared Goff, QBDetroit Lions Brady: "Jared Goff. I've covered him now in back-to-back weeks. Total command of the offense. Doing such a great job distributing the ball, deep to Jameson Williams, to Amon-Ra [St. Brown]. He's got it all going." Stats: 1,964 passing yards, 15 touchdown passes, one interception and a 110.0 passer rating (through seven games). Odds: At +2700, Goff holds the seventh-best odds. Goff has never finished higher than five in MVP voting, but this season, he's on track for a career-high 4,770 passing yards. articles.title: Australia appoint Mike Hussey as consultant for Ashes and Cricket World Cup
articles.summary: Hussey, known as ‘Mr Cricket’ for his technical expertise, will also work with Australia during the LA 2028 Olympics.
articles.body:
Mike Hussey was appointed on Friday as a consultant coach to the Australian team for next year’s blockbuster Ashes series against England and the 2027 Cricket World Cup .

The former Australian batsman revealed in August that England’s new red-ball coach, Stephen Fleming, had informally approached him to be their Test batting mentor.

But the 51-year-old turned down the audacious offer and has instead committed to helping his home nation arrest a batting crisis, highlighted by their recent 2-1 Test series defeat in South Africa.

Hussey, known as “Mr Cricket” for his technical expertise, will also provide coaching assistance during this month’s home T20 series against England and the subsequent four-Test series against New Zealand.

He will additionally work with Australia during the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics , where cricket is on the agenda, and the T20 World Cup in 2028.

“I am extremely excited about being a part of the team in a more formal and meaningful role in the coming years,” said Hussey, who played more than 300 matches for Australia across all formats.

“This team has achieved so much in recent times, to which I hope I can add value to the coaching and playing groups ahead of what will be an exciting and challenging period.”

Hussey has extensive experience as a coach, including with both Australia and England.

He was part of England’s coaching setup when they won the T20 World Cup in 2022 and was the Chennai Super Kings’ longtime batting coach under Fleming in the Indian Premier League. He also led Welsh Fire in this year’s Hundred.

“Mike has been a highly valued part of our staff in the past and brings a considerable skill set which is complementary to the coaches and players,” said Australian head coach Andrew McDonald.

“Not only is his expertise as a player and coach across multiple formats, competitions, countries invaluable, so are his qualities as a person.”

articles.title: El YangWang U9 Xtreme supera los 500 km/h: este es el nuevo récord mundial de velocidad
articles.standfirst: El Yangwang U9 Xtreme ha alcanzado los 503,17 km/h en una carretera de Abu Dabi y la marca china ha convertido el edificio más alto del mundo en el escenario de su celebración.
articles.summary: El Yangwang U9 Xtreme ha alcanzado los 503,17 km/h en una carretera de Abu Dabi y la marca china ha convertido el edificio más alto del mundo en el escenario de su celebración.
articles.body: Se quedó a las puertas, pero ahora BYD lo ha conseguido. Su hiperdeportivo eléctrico Yangwang U9 Xtreme ha superado la barrera de los 500 km/h, una velocidad inalcanzable hasta ahora para cualquier supercoche del planeta: ni Porsche, ni Ferrari, ni Bugatti fueron capaces de lograr lo que acaba de conseguir la marca china. El Yangwang U9 Xtreme ha alcanzado los 503,17 km/h, una cifra con la que ha batido su propio récord mundial de velocidad (496, 22) y que BYD va a celebrar a lo grande en Dubái, con un espectacular despliegue de luces y proyecciones sobre el Burj Khalifa, el edificio más alto del mundo. La hazaña tuvo lugar el pasado 1 de noviembre en Abu Dabi, concretamente en un tramo de la carretera Sheikh Khalifa Bin Zayed (E11), en la región de Al Dhafra. Allí, el piloto alemán Marc Basseng llevó al Yangwang U9 Xtreme hasta los 503,17 km/h, superando la barrera psicológica de los 500 km/h que ya rozaron en su primer intento, en septiembre de 2025, por entonces en la pista de pruebas de Papenburg (Alemania). Según comunica BYD, el registro le ha permitido conseguir dos nuevos récords Guinness: el de mayor velocidad alcanzada por un coche de producción en una pasada en un solo sentido y el equivalente para un automóvil eléctrico de producción. La marca asegura también que la velocidad ha sido reconocida por la Federación Internacional del Automóvil (FIA). Se trata de un matiz importante, ya que el registro corresponde a una velocidad máxima en una única dirección, y no a una media obtenida mediante dos pasadas en sentidos opuestos, como sucede en otros tipos de récords de velocidad. Pero BYD no quería que semejante hazaña pasara desapercibida. Por eso, la compañía eligió Dubái y su edificio más emblemático, el Burj Khalifa, para celebrar el récord en un evento al que asistirán alrededor de 3.000 invitados, entre representantes de medios internacionales y personalidades de todo el mundo. El rascacielos, de 828 metros de altura, se convertirá en una gigantesca pantalla sobre la que se proyectará un espectáculo de luces e imágenes dedicado al Yangwang U9 Xtreme y a su histórica marca de velocidad. Una celebración con la que el gigante chino pretende demostrar que su tecnología eléctrica no solo sirve para desarrollar vehículos eficientes, sino también para competir en prestaciones con los superdeportivos más exclusivos del mundo. La celebración servirá, además para reconocer otro de los logros recientes de BYD, distinguida como Marca del Año en la categoría de Automóviles, a nivel global, en los World Branding Awards. Su vicepresidenta ejecutiva, Stella Li, destacó el significado de los 503,17 km/h del U9 Xtreme, una cifra que, según la directiva, demuestra hasta dónde pueden llegar las prestaciones de un automóvil eléctrico y la ambición de los ingenieros de la compañía. Las celebraciones continuarán el 7 de noviembre en Abu Dabi, donde BYD ha organizado un desfile con 110 vehículos de sus marcas BYD, Denza y Yangwang, encabezado precisamente por el U9 Xtreme, que recorrerá el trayecto entre West Park y Emirates Palace.

articles.title: 2026-27 FA Cup: What is the prize money, TV bonus, gate receipts?
articles.summary: Our Ask Me Anything team look at what teams could be set to earn from the 2026-27 FA Cup.
articles.body:
It's not just the glory of a historic trophy that appeals to teams competing in the FA Cup.

The world's oldest national football tournament can provide a significant financial boost to lower-league clubs.

With the Football Association's participation prize money on offer for both losers and winners at nearly every round, as well as lucrative TV bonuses and gate fees on top, there are big monetary incentives for smaller teams to progress as far as possible.

A total of 743 teams entered the men's competition and 535 entered the women's tournament - so how is the money allocated to them all?

Men's and women's FA Cup prize money breakdown

Including preliminary and qualifying rounds, there are a total of 14 rounds in the men's FA Cup, with prizes for both the winners and losers in all but three matches.

All twelve rounds in the women's FA Cup have participation fees for both the winners and losers.

How much do teams get for appearing on TV in the FA Cup?

Eight matches have been chosen for live TV coverage in the men's first round, with two being shown on the BBC.

The 16 clubs taking part in these fixtures will receive a live television broadcast fee of £50,000 on top of their participation fees.

Broadcast fees increase as the tournament progresses, with third-round payments of £80,000 per club being paid in 2025-26, once Premier League teams entered the competition, rising to £120,000 by the fifth round.

Broadcast rights for the Women's FA Cup are shared by TNT Sports and Channel 4, with Women's Super League clubs entering in the fourth round.

How do teams split gate receipts in the FA Cup?

Under FA Cup rules, funds from gate receipts are shared equally between the two clubs - after certain hosting costs are taken out.

It means lower league clubs can potentially get a significant financial boost by being drawn away against a Premier League side from the third round onward.

articles.title: España no se deja intimidar por Argentina en el Mundial de pádel: "No hay un favorito claro"
articles.standfirst: Juanjo Gutiérrez y Arturo Coello defienden sus opciones ante la albiceleste pese a la baja de Ale Galán.
articles.summary: Juanjo Gutiérrez y Arturo Coello defienden sus opciones ante la albiceleste pese a la baja de Ale Galán.
articles.body: Con la baja de Ale Galán para el Mundial de pádel, la selección argentina parece tener más opciones de salir campeona del torneo en una hipotética final ante España. Sin embargo, tanto el seleccionador nacional, Juanjo Gutiérrez, como Arturo Coello, una de las principales figuras del equipo, han querido defender sus opciones en la rueda de prensa posterior a los cuartos de final frente a Brasil. Juanjo aseguró que sigue existiendo mucha igualdad: “Yo creo que no hay un favorito claro. Depende mucho de cómo caigan los enfrentamientos y cómo se encuentran ese día los jugadores. Todos se conocen muchísimo, es un deporte que influye mucho en los estados de ánimo, y sobre todo el timing con el que lleguen. Así que creo que se decidirá por detalles”. El ‘King’, por su parte, fue más tajante: “Somos nosotros favoritos”. Precisamente el vallisoletano habló sobre su papel en la convocatoria, siendo todavía joven pero el integrante con mejor ranking: “No, no me siento líder. Si lidero en ocasiones es totalmente involuntario por mi personalidad. No trato de llevar la batuta del equipo, ni mucho menos, soy una persona que se mantiene bastante al margen de eso. Trato de aportar lo que puedo, de ayudar al que pide mi ayuda, pero me mantengo bastante al margen. Creo que hay en este equipo personalidades con una influencia mayor, como pueden ser Paco o Juan, que son personas que están más en el liderazgo y en ese tipo de cosas; yo soy más tranquilo en ese aspecto. Mi idea no es liderar, es ser uno más y aportar mi granito de arena”. Juanjo también alabó entre risas la figura de Paquito Navarro: “Cuando empezó a jugar, Javi no sabía ni lo que era el pádel. No existía. Por lo tanto, Paco es como esa persona que tiene 2.000 años y sigue compitiendo. Él hace un poco de nexo de unión entre las generaciones y es verdad porque ha vivido tres generaciones. Así que por suerte la base se mantiene”. Un ambiente que también ha valorado muy positivamente Javi Leal: “Es una semana en la que tenemos la opción de disfrutar de mucha gente y de poder conversar con personas que quizás en el año no tienes tanta posibilidad de hablar y también nutrirte de ver ciertas cosas, de ver cómo ciertos jugadores entrenan y cómo piensan. Aparte, todos tenemos el mismo objetivo y todos representamos y defendemos los mismos valores y las mismas ilusiones, con lo cual estamos muy contentos”. Una de las grandes dudas de la semana es la formación que elegirá Juanjo Gutiérrez, quien no ha desvelado ninguna pincelada sobre qué jugadores o el orden que pondrá en el cruce definitivo: “Sí, evidentemente ya tengo una idea más o menos armada y ahora faltan pues detalles. No te puedo dar más información. Lamentablemente no te puedo dar más información”. Sin embargo, reconoció que fueron precisamente Javi Leal y Arturo Coello los que más le han sorprendido juntos sobre la pista. Además, pese a que España ha superado las rondas con la facilidad esperada, Gutiérrez explicó que sus jugadores sienten ya esa emoción y presión propias de estar cerca del momento decisivo: “Creo que el equipo sigue manteniendo esa línea de trabajo bueno, de muchísima química, y hoy lo he hablado con Nacho, mi preparador; cuando he llegado al gimnasio por la mañana he visto otras caras, he visto unas caras distintas, he visto unas miradas totalmente cambiadas”. En semifinales se medirán a Portugal, mientras que Argentina lo hará con Italia. En cualquier caso, ambos combinados se dirigen al desenlace más ansiado: volver a verse las caras por el campeonato del mundo dos años después.

articles.title: Delhi HC finds ‘Doosra’ prima facie infringes Sourav Ganguly’s personality rights, orders makers to furnish Rs 2 crore bank guarantee
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court on Friday held that the film Doosra prima facie violated former India captain Sourav Ganguly’s personality and publicity
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Delhi High Court on Friday held that the film Doosra prima facie violated former India captain Sourav Ganguly’s personality and publicity rights, directing its producers to furnish an unconditional bank guarantee of Rs 2 crore while refusing to halt the film’s theatrical run.Justice Tejas Karia observed that Ganguly’s personality and publicity rights were so intertwined with the story of the film that it would not be feasible to remove the infringing portions. The court, however, stopped short of granting Ganguly’s request to restrain the film’s release and commercial exhibition.As per Bar and Bench report, the court directed Ramesh Deo Productions Private Limited, the makers of Doosra, to furnish the bank guarantee with the registrar within two weeks. It also ordered the producers to carry disclaimers in both Hindi and English at the beginning and end of the film within two days of the order.The disclaimers must clearly state that Ganguly had not consented to the use of his persona in the film and that the movie was not intended to violate his personality and publicity rights.The court warned that failure to comply with any of the conditions would result in the makers and anyone acting on their behalf being restrained from making commercial use of the film or any of its aspects.Ganguly objects to use of NatWest final, iconic Lord's celebrationThe order came on a plea filed by Ganguly and Luv Films LLP, which sought to restrain the theatrical, digital and other releases of Doosra, along with the circulation of promotional material allegedly using the former cricketer’s name, image, likeness and iconic career moments without authorisation.At the centre of the dispute are references to Ganguly’s captaincy and India's historic victory in the 2002 NatWest series final against England at Lord’s, including his famous shirtless celebration on the balcony. Ganguly and Luv Films alleged that the film and its promotional campaign commercially exploited his identity and reputation, potentially creating an impression that he was associated with or had endorsed the project.They also cited the film’s trailer and promotional campaign, launched on October 12, as well as an October 13 interview in which director Abhinay Deo discussed how the NatWest final and milestones in Ganguly’s career had influenced the film’s fictional character, Tara.Dispute over exclusive rights to Ganguly biopicThe suit also raised a contractual dispute between Ganguly and Luv Films. According to the petition, Ganguly entered into an agreement with the production house on August 5, 2021, granting it exclusive rights to develop, produce and commercially exploit audiovisual content, including a biographical film based on his life and cricketing career.Luv Films claimed to have made substantial investments in the authorised biopic, titled Dada – The Sourav Ganguly Story, which is scheduled for release on May 14, 2027.The petitioners argued that Doosra's references to Ganguly’s career and iconic moments amounted to unauthorised commercial exploitation of his personality rights and infringed the production house’s exclusive contractual rights over the proposed biopic.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Rugby League World Cup 2026: England top group en route to World Cup semis
articles.summary: England captain Lewis King says his side relish "high-pressure games" after they beat Ireland to secure top spot in Pool A en route to the semi-finals of the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup.
articles.body:
England captain Lewis King says his side relish "high-pressure games" after they claimed a 68-32 victory over Ireland to secure top spot in Pool A en route to the semi-finals of the Wheelchair Rugby League World Cup.

Joe Coyd (with four) and Rob Hawkins (with three) scored seven of England's 12 tries with Mason Billington and King twice crossing and Jack Brown the other try scorer for the reigning champions at the Wollongong Entertainment Arena.

The result means England head into their last-four meeting with co-hosts Australia on Tuesday (08:45 GMT) with a 100% record, having thrashed Wales and the USA in the group stage.

However, they were far from comfortable against an Ireland side who led 14-0 and 20-4 during the first half before England recovered to take a 22-20 advantage into the break.

"We knew it was going to be a challenge and our biggest in the tournament so far but that is why we are here. We love these high-pressure games," King told Premier Sports.

"Massive respect to Ireland. They came out strong and we had to ride the wave of penalties. Eventually we got through it. It was a great game.

"We had to build ourselves into the game and we did that at the beginning of the second half and we found our groove and a way to win."

In contrast to the first period when Ireland dominated possession, England piled on 40 unanswered points after the break before Ireland crossed again.

However, King was far from satisfied with their overall showing.

"We will concentrate on us. We won't be particularly pleased with our performance today. Our standards are higher," he added.

"We topped the group and that was the first aim. We have done that and we'll take that momentum into next week."

In a repeat of their last-four meeting from four years ago, France pulled clear of the Wheelaroos after a tight opening 40 minutes to win 69-34 and top their group.

The runners-up in 2022, twice winners of the competition, will take on Ireland on Tuesday (06:15 GMT) looking to book a place in their fourth consecutive final.

Earlier on Friday, Calum Davidson scored four tries as Scotland defeated New Zealand 62-18 to record their first-ever win at a Wheelchair World Cup.

"We knew it was there but we tried to not make it a big thing," he said. "The fact we have done it is amazing.

"It is just going to keep getting better and better for us."

Wales also triumphed, 92-18 against the USA, with John Berriman scoring four tries and Fionn McCabe and Jonathan Gill both grabbing hat-tricks to boost confidence prior to the play-off matches for positions five to eight.

articles.title: Nigerian blind sambo champion Rukayat Taiwo Suleimon makes history for Africa
articles.summary: After losing her sight in 2009, Nigeria’s Rukayat Suleimon has overcome isolation and limited support to make history as the first blind woman to win gold at the World Sambo Cup.
articles.body:
Rukayat Taiwo Suleimon only took up sambo this year, but the Nigerian has already secured her place in the history of the martial art.

The sport shares strong roots with judo and wrestling, combining techniques such as hip and leg throws to take opponents to the mat, where they can be pinned.

Originally developed by the Soviet Union's Red Army in the 1920s, it was officially recognised as a combat sport by USSR officials in 1938.

Competing at the 2026 World Sambo Cup in Armenia, Suleimon defeated Uzbekistan's Charos Ortikova in the final of the women's 54kg category to claim victory on her international debut.

It was the first time that women with visual impairments had been included at the competition.

"Being the first female blind sambist in the world to win the gold medal makes me great," the 32-year-old told BBC Sport Africa.

"This is my first time in sambo and God crowned my efforts."

Suleimon's achievement was part of a breakthrough moment for African women in the sport. She and compatriot Elizabeth Aseso, who competed in the 59kg category, were among the pioneering sambists representing the continent in Yerevan.

For Suleimon, her gold medal is a reward for the hard work over many years which has seen her move from athletics to judo and now to the top of the international sambo podium.

"I really benefit a lot from sports and, despite my blindness, I achieve a lot," she said.

"If I [were] not blind, I don't think I would be at this level. I believe I will achieve even more."

Suleimon's journey to becoming a champion has been marked by hardship and a determination to rebuild her life.

After failed surgeries she lost her sight in 2009 because of glaucoma, an eye condition that damages the optic nerve and can lead to permanent loss of vision.

The change in her circumstances affected her relationships, leaving her feeling isolated at a time when she needed support the most.

"People looked down on me. I would just stay indoors and cry," she explained.

"So many friends left me. They stopped communicating with me."

Her life began to take a different direction after she attended a vocational training centre for blind people in Lagos.

Through a friend, she was introduced to a para-athletics coach who helped her discover her potential in sport.

Since 2011, Suleimon has won more than 20 national medals across sprint events (alongside guide runner Stephen Oyelakin), discus and shot put.

She then began practicing judo and sambo.

"Since I [started] sports I have seen that where there is life, there is hope," she said.

"What sighted people can do, a blind person can do even better.

"I'm proud of myself because it's not easy to be a champion in athletics and in sambo. I don't want to lose the glory."

Her achievements have also become a source of pride for her family. Her twin sister Ganiyat Kehinde Suleimon says her sibling's disability has never defined her worth.

"She is someone we are all proud of. She is now a champion," Ganiyat told BBC Sport Africa.

"Her disability did not make her a liability to us."

For Nigerian sambo coach Olugbenga Adekahunsi, Suleimon's performance in Yerevan offered a glimpse of what she can accomplish with the right support and continued development.

"I see a lot of quality in her because she is very strong and the confidence is there," he told BBC Sport Africa.

"I believe she will become a great sambist."

Suleimon says the recognition she has earned internationally has not been matched by adequate "support" at home.

However, her victory is the latest milestone in Nigeria's growing presence in the discipline.

Two years ago Samuel Oladele Kekere became the first blind African to compete at the World Sambo Championships in Kazakhstan, and Sodiq Ajibade followed that with a bronze medal at last year's edition in Kyrgyzstan.

"Despite making Nigeria and the whole of Africa proud, there is nothing to show for it," Suleimon said.

Her concerns reflect wider complaints from Nigerian para-athletes about limited funding, inadequate specialist facilities and insufficient institutional backing, despite their achievements.

Sherif Hammed, vice-president of the Sambo Association of Nigeria, says a lack of resources can prevent talented athletes from reaching their full potential.

"When athletes do not have facilities to train, they cannot compete at the world level," he said.

"It is quite disheartening and heartbreaking.

"People with disabilities, particularly visually impaired athletes, sometimes feel that because of their challenges, they have no purpose in life."

For Suleimon, a Lagos State judo champion, the journey to training is also an issue. Travelling across the city and covering transport costs make maintaining a demanding schedule difficult.

"I leave home at 5.30am to make it to training on time," she explained.

"It takes a lot of money and sacrifice."

Suleimon was unable to follow up her World Cup success at the World Sambo Championships in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, where blind women were again scheduled to compete for the first time.

Beaten in Friday's opening round by Moldova's Ina Cernei, she still hopes her exploits on the global stage can inspire others.

"I want to encourage my fellow blind Africans to believe they can do it," said Suleimon. "And I want to make my country proud again."

articles.summary: The Diyarbakir-based club have risen from the third tier to a top-of-the-table clash in the Turkish Super Lig.
articles.body:
Ten years ago, as parts of Diyarbakir in southeast Turkiye were reduced to rubble in battles between the military and Kurdish fighters, the city’s main football club, Amedspor, became a target.

Diyarbakir is the biggest Kurdish-majority city in Turkiye, and Amedspor , then in the third tier, had become a standard bearer of Kurdish identity.

As fighting raged between the state and groups linked to the outlawed Kurdistan Workers’ Party (PKK), the club was hit with fines and bans on away supporters and outspoken players. Its premises were raided by antiterrorism police, and its fans, players and officials were attacked by rival supporters. In the years that followed, its survival looked uncertain.

A decade on, a peace process is under way between the government and the PKK, and Amedspor – in their first season in the top-flight after successive promotions – are second in the Super Lig after 10 games. A win at league leaders Galatasaray on Saturday would take them to the top.

“Amedspor have achieved a level of success that nobody expected,” said Vahap Coskun, an academic from Diyarbakir who has written a book about the club.

Coskun told Al Jazeera there are several factors behind the success this season; an experienced and canny coach in Besnik Hasi, and a mostly new squad of players performing above expectations, including the 24-year-old Nigerian striker Gift Orban, who has scored nine goals in 10 games so far.

Then there are the passionate, sellout crowds of more than 30,000 that have helped the side win its six home games so far.

But he also said the “softening political climate” was key as it “affects everything from the treatment Amedspor receive in away matches to the refereeing, and it allows Amedspor to compete in fairer conditions”.

Reha Ruhavioglu, director of the Kurdish Studies Center (KSC) and a former member of the club’s advisory board, told Al Jazeera Amedspor’s matches have become a “weekly barometer” of whether Turkish society and state can accept the club as part of the country “with its own colours, culture, language and identity”.

Amedspor was formed as Melikahmet Turanspor in 1972 and later passed through various name changes and was taken over by Diyarbakir’s municipality in 1990. They spent much of their history toiling in the lower leagues.

The club gained promotion to the third tier for the first time in 2013, and the following year caused a stir after renaming themselves with the Kurdish word for Diyarbakir – “Amed” – and adopting the red, green and yellow of the Kurdish tricolour.

Expressions of Kurdish culture and language have long been suppressed in Turkiye, especially after the separatist PKK launched an armed uprising against the Turkish state in 1984. But the club were allowed to use the name Amed and their green and red colours at least, if not the full tricolour.

They were clearly on the up. In January 2015, they claimed a 2-0 victory away at Galatasaray in the Turkish Cup. In 2015-16, as conflict raged in Turkiye’s southeast, they reached the quarterfinals of the Turkish Cup, beating Super Lig sides Basaksehir and Bursaspor along the way.

In the following years, the club was bailed out by local businesses after its funding was cut by government appointees to the municipality. It continued to face significant hostility from rival fans, frequent punishment from the federation and verbal attacks from politicians.

But it was becoming increasingly popular among Kurds across the country, not only in Diyarbakir.

Research published by the KSC in March 2026 found that Amedspor’s support had quadrupled to four million among Kurdish adults in Turkiye over four years – even before the promotion to the Super Lig – and that the club had become the best supported among Kurds in the country.

Meanwhile, a new peace process between the state and the PKK had begun in late 2024, and in May 2025 the PKK formally announced its dissolution and the end of its armed struggle.

When Amedspor were promoted to the Super Lig in May, President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his ultranationalist ally Devlet Bahceli congratulated the club. Erdogan later received Amedspor officials and players at the presidential palace along with those from other promoted clubs.

Bagis Erten, a sports journalist with Oksijen newspaper, said that now the political winds have shifted, the club is not being held back or excessively punished by footballing authorities.

“Especially when we talk about the football federation and referees, [Amedspor] were always treated very badly in previous years. Their penalties were not given, their red cards were not fair,” he told Al Jazeera.

“But now this system at least is not stopping them.”

At Amedspor’s Diyarbakir Stadium, the crowd in one stand calls out in Kurdish: “Ki ne em?” (Who are we?). Another stand thunders in response: “Kurd in em!” (We are Kurds!) At a recent game against Istanbul giants Besiktas, which Amedspor won 3-2, a tifo featured the words “EM HATIN” (We are here).

Turkish society is now encountering the Kurdish language and other expressions of Kurdish identity more regularly because of Amedspor’s promotion to the Super Lig.

There has been hostility shown by rival fans this season, with some provocatively displaying yellow body bags and images of F16s in reference to the darkest days of the conflict with the PKK.

But Ruhavioglu says that, despite incidents like this, the “barometer” is generally looking positive and that football can help to “normalise” Kurdish identity in Turkiye, as several teams and their fans have now visited the city without incident.

“When you see the bigger picture, it is going well,” he said.

Ruhavioglu says his centre’s research has also challenged some misconceptions around the club and its fans.

“Amedspor’s stands are really not homogenous,” he said, adding that while many fans support the left-wing, pro-Kurdish DEM Party, others are “close to other parties and ideologies. The Kurdish political movement is [generally] a secular movement, but many fans are praying in the stadium.”

And although the research found that a sense of Kurdishness and speaking Kurdish were strongly tied to fandom of Amedspor, he said the club should not be seen as “a national team for Kurds”, but rather more like “the representative of Kurdish identity” in Turkiye. Indeed, 61 percent of Kurds in the survey said they support the Turkish national team when it plays.

Unlike when the club was playing in the lower tiers, Amedspor now rarely features Kurdish or local players in the starting XI – it is mostly comprised of foreign players and some non-Kurdish Turks.

Coskun denied this undermines the club’s sense of Kurdishness.

“I think the fact that few of the players are Kurdish is not of vital importance to the fans, because it is the club that carries the identity, not the players,” he said. “Of course, fans would like to see many more Kurdish players in the team, but what matters most here is success.”

But Erten says the club may end up seeking to dilute its political identity to pursue footballing success or at least avoid trouble.

“Of course, it’s the symbol of Kurdish movement … [but] they are trying to convince Turkish society that it’s a good football project as well.”

Erten says attitudes towards Amedspor show how Turkiye’s state and society have become more tolerant of prominent expressions of Kurdishness on a national level, something that was unthinkable in previous decades.

“It’s progress, but it depends only on the approach of government,” he said. “It’s very fragile progress.”

articles.title: Final Picks for Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn and Entire WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Match Card
articles.summary: WWE Crown Jewel 2026 will feature four matches, including a blockbuster showdown between Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn.
articles.body:
WWE Crown Jewel 2026 will feature four matches, including a blockbuster showdown between Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn.

Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton will meet in a Last Man Standing match, while Liv Morgan, Chelsea Green, and two tag teams will also compete for championship gold.

Here's the full match card, along with my predicted winners in italics:

Predicting Next Year's Crown Jewel Matches 🔮

2026 WWE Men's Crown Jewel Championship: Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn

2026 WWE Women's Crown Jewel Championship: Liv Morgan vs. Chelsea Green

Last Man Standing match: Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton

World Tag Team Championship: Bron Breakker and Austin Theory vs. Penta and Je'Von Evans

Zayn has a chance to score the biggest victory of his career in front of a Crown Jewel crowd firmly in his corner, but taking down Reigns is an entirely different challenge.

The former Honorary Uce knows Reigns better than almost anyone, and their history should add another interesting layer to what is already one of the more compelling matchups on the card.

Unfortunately for Zayn, WWE has never been particularly subtle about protecting its biggest attractions, and there's little reason to believe the company is ready to change that philosophy.

Reigns should ultimately have too much for Zayn, picking up another high-profile victory while leaving his former ally searching for an answer.

Rhodes and Orton have years of history between them, and their latest confrontation should give both men plenty of opportunities to get extremely violent.

The Last Man Standing stipulation is a fitting addition to this rivalry, especially considering how personal things have become between the former mentor and protégé.

Orton has the experience and ruthlessness to make life miserable for Rhodes, but WWE has invested far too much in The American Nightmare to have him come up short here.

Expect Rhodes to survive another brutal encounter and put The Viper down for the count.

Green has spent most of her WWE run proving she's one of the most entertaining performers on the roster, even when the creative direction seems determined to turn her into a walking punchline.

Morgan is an accomplished competitor who knows what it takes to win on a big stage, but Green deserves recognition as more than a comedic side character.

A victory at Crown Jewel would be a meaningful step forward for Green and give WWE a chance to do something different with its championship picture.

I'm taking Green to pull off the upset, capture the Women's Crown Jewel Championship, and remind everyone that she's capable of being much more than a joke.

Bron Breakker and Austin Theory vs. Penta and Je'Von Evans

Breakker and Theory have been a strong combination for The Vision, but this feels like the right time for a change. Penta and Evans bring an exciting mix of experience, athleticism, and high-flying ability that could make them an entertaining championship team.

Breakker also seems destined for bigger opportunities as a singles competitor, making this a good opportunity to move the tag titles elsewhere without hurting his momentum. Theory can take the fall while Breakker moves on to bigger things. Look for a title change and a new championship team.

For more wrestling talk, listen to Ring Rust Radio for all of the hot topics or catch the latest episode in the player above (some language NSFW).

articles.title: Updated 2026 WWE Crown Jewel Card and Predictions for Match Order
articles.summary: The top champions in both the men's and women's divisions will clash on Saturday when the Crown Jewel premium live event emanates from Saudi Arabia.
articles.body:
The top champions in both the men's and women's divisions will clash on Saturday when the Crown Jewel premium live event emanates from Saudi Arabia.

Saturday's card will be headlined by the Crown Jewel Championship match between world heavyweight champion Roman Reigns and WWE champion Sami Zayn, as well as the Women's Crown Jewel Championship bout pitting women's world champion Liv Morgan against WWE women's champion Chelsea Green.

On top of that, Randy Orton and Cody Rhodes are set to do battle in a Last Man Standing match, and The Vision's Bron Breakker and Austin Theory will defend the World Tag Team Championships against Penta and Je'Von Evans.

Predicting Next Year's Crown Jewel Matches 🔮

Here is all the information you need ahead of Crown Jewel, including a look at the entire card and projected match order.

Where: ANB Arena in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia

WWE Crown Jewel 2026 Card and Projected Match Order

World Tag Team Championships: The Vision (Bron Breakker & Austin Theory) (c) vs. Penta & Je'Von Evans

Last Man Standing: Cody Rhodes vs. Randy Orton

Women's Crown Jewel Championship: Liv Morgan vs. Chelsea Green

Crown Jewel Championship: Roman Reigns vs. Sami Zayn

In what figures to be the main event of the show, Roman Reigns and Sami Zayn will renew their rivalry with the Crown Jewel Championship hanging in the balance.

Zayn was once the Honorary Uce of The Bloodline, and he played a significant role in the group's success, as well as the lengthy run Reigns enjoyed as WWE champion.

However, Zayn eventually turned on Reigns and The Bloodline when they attacked Kevin Owens, making him The Bloodline's public enemy No. 1 for quite some time.

They have since gone their separate ways completely, and Zayn has come into his own as a top star and main eventer, holding the WWE Championship twice this year.

Reigns has been preoccupied with 946 leading up to Crown Jewel, causing Zayn to remain The OTC how big of a threat he truly is.

The looming presence of 946 suggests that Zayn could pull off the upset, and that possibility adds to the intrigue of what already looks to be a highly compelling encounter.

A rivalry that has been going since before WrestleMania 42 may very well get settled once and for all at Crown Jewel.

Cody Rhodes and Randy Orton have split their past two meetings with Rhodes winning at WrestleMania, and Orton getting some revenge at Sunday Night's Main Event in September.

Their feud has been a highly personal one with both Rhodes and Orton evoking the names of family members and doing everything possible to gain a mental edge.

At Crown Jewel, The American Nightmare and The Viper will do battle in one of the most brutal match types in all of wrestling.

Pinfalls and submissions are no longer enough to decide things, which is why the winner must keep their opponent down for the count of 10 at Crown Jewel.

Liv Morgan will have a chance to become the first-ever two-time women's Crown Jewel champion when she faces Chelsea Green on Saturday.

Morgan became the first women's Crown Jewel champion two years ago, and she has momentum on her side entering Crown Jewel 2026 after pinning Green in a six-woman tag team match on Raw.

Liv also has the benefit of The Judgment Day backing her up, although Chelsea has been getting some help lately as well from the likes of Tiffany Stratton and Iyo Sky.

Stratton's presence could throw a wrench into things, as she has teased cashing in her Money in the Bank contract on Morgan multiple times already.

That possibility looms at Crown Jewel, as does the possibility of Tiffany double-crossing Green and cashing in on her instead.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo: Portugal’s polarising icon and his bitter final act
articles.summary: After announcing his international retirement, Portugal’s longstanding captain leaves behind a complicated legacy.
articles.body:
An inviting volley blazed over the bar, a trademark free kick clattering into the wall, and a showman’s celebrations cut short by an offside goal.

In many ways, the frustrations Cristiano Ronaldo endured in his final match for Portugal reflected his long-altered reality – one of football’s most devastating players had become a liability.

For many, Ronaldo’s fall from grace could hardly be crueller.

The boy from Madeira captivated the world for years with his jaw-dropping talent, age-defying athleticism and larger-than-life personality. Yet the final chapter of his international career had anything but a fairytale ending – a forgettable climax to an otherwise illustrious journey.

Ronaldo has walked away from the national team with individual achievements most footballers can only dream of: the all-time record for international appearances (234) and goals (146).

“Portugal will always be a part of me,” the 41-year-old said in a five-minute video shared on Thursday, bidding goodbye to the team he first played for in 2003.

But his international retirement was hardly a surprise.

In the weeks leading up to his announcement, Ronaldo had been at the centre of a controversy , leaving fans and critics wondering if that was the end of the road for Portugal’s longstanding captain.

The forward’s waning influence on the field, a public rift with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus and a near 2,000-word statement after a dramatic mid-camp walkout were the perfect recipe for worldwide football gossip – and ultimately, retirement.

“He wanted the manager to go out and say ‘I’ve put a player on the bench at the calibre of Pele and [Diego] Maradona,'” ex-Liverpool player-turned-pundit Jamie Carragher said on The Overlap podcast.

“How do you say that about yourself? It’s mad, isn’t it?”

For more than two decades, Ronaldo made himself impossible to ignore in a Portugal shirt. He brought home the Selecao’s first major trophy, the Euro 2016 crown, before adding two Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025.

After being celebrated as a hero, Ronaldo slowly transitioned into the villain during the World Cup in Qatar. A lack of goals saw him dropped to the bench in two crucial knockout games, while his performances and attitude drew criticism as Portugal were sent packing in the quarterfinals.

The script repeated itself at Euro 2024 before the FIFA World Cup 2026 marked his final appearance on the sport’s biggest stage – the forward scoring three times, including his first and only World Cup knockout goal.

He bowed out of the biggest World Cup in North America as the first player to score in six editions, but those personal landmarks never translated into the trophy he sought. Portugal lost to eventual champions Spain in the last 16, and with that, Ronaldo’s dream of being crowned a world champion remained unfulfilled.

“I won Euro 2016 and, for me, that’s just as important as the World Cup. It will stay with me forever,” the five-time Ballon d’Or winner said this year, seemingly making peace with the bitter ending.

For much of his career, Ronaldo drew constant comparisons with Argentinian legend Lionel Messi; the duo igniting the debate for the “greatest of all time” (GOAT). It was, thus, rather poetic that Ronaldo followed Messi’s suit in hanging up his boots at the international level.

But there is a striking contrast in their farewells. Messi’s send-off was marked with celebrations after he guided Argentina to a second straight World Cup final . Ronaldo, on the other hand, is leaving the scene after a rather tense span in the Portugal camp, and probably without a proper goodbye on the field.

Nonetheless, Ronaldo’s announcement drew an outpouring of affection from fans and figures across the football fraternity.

Often described as a childhood idol by several teammates at club or country, Ronaldo is one of the most famous people on the planet.

Walk around your nearest park, and you’re likely to spot a kid dressed in a “Ronaldo 7” jersey, kicking a ball around.

A commercial powerhouse for his national team and clubs alike, Ronaldo’s popularity transcended sports.

“Few ‌players have ever touched the heart of football fans around the world quite like Cristiano,” FIFA President Gianni Infantino said about him.

“A career defined by extraordinary talent, relentless determination and an unwavering desire to push the boundaries of what is possible.”

While his tricks and skills earned him the honour of one of the greatest players of all time, Ronaldo’s on-field antics and perceived arrogance divided opinion in the football world.

In a recent interview with The Athletic, ex-Manchester United manager Erik ten Hag discussed his issues involving Ronaldo, alleging that the forward pulled out of training sessions during his second spell at the club and failed to raise his heart rate to the required level when he did train.

“I confronted him with this. Many times, I say, ‘Ronnie, everyone wants to work for you to bring you in the right position, but if you can’t bring yourself in the box, you can’t score’,” Ten Hag said.

“He was not capable to do this. It’s the wrong idea to put this to me that I expected him to do the pressing, that he’s exhausted. But he couldn’t. He ran neither in possession nor out of possession. The reason was because he didn’t prepare himself.

“Every top team has to embrace the top player, but the top player has to work for the team,” Ten Hag added.

While some saw Ronaldo as the icon who transformed Portuguese football, others questioned his individualism.

The debate over how best to define him will continue for years, but one thing is certain: Ronaldo’s complex legacy is perhaps summed up by his former club Man United’s famous slogan: “Hated, adored, never ignored”.

articles.title: Portugal FA pledges to honour Cristiano Ronaldo as Jorge Jesus names squad
articles.summary: Portuguese FA promises to celebrate Ronaldo, although it is unclear whether he ⁠would agree to a farewell appearance.
articles.body:
Portugal has pledged to ‌honour Cristiano Ronaldo as manager Jorge Jesus named his first squad ⁠since the captain’s ⁠international retirement, then faced a barrage of questions about the rift that preceded the departure.

The 41-year-old announced his decision to retire on social media on Thursday, ⁠ending a Portugal career spanning 234 appearances and 146 goals.

Portuguese FA president Pedro Proenca promised to celebrate Ronaldo’s contribution, although there was no word on whether the forward ⁠would agree to a farewell appearance.

“No tribute will ever be enough to thank him for everything he has done for Portuguese football, for Portugal,” Proenca said before the squad announcement on Friday.

“We will do everything we can to honour the legacy he leaves us. Everything he has ‌done deserves to be honoured and celebrated.”

Jesus selected seven new faces, including five players from the under-21s, for November’s Nations League matches against Wales and Denmark, but Ronaldo’s absence from the squad dominated proceedings.

The forward left Portugal’s camp without permission at the end of September, ahead of a Nations League match against Denmark, and did not return. He later cited broken promises from Jesus as the reason for his departure.

Jesus became visibly ⁠annoyed as journalists pressed him about the dispute, repeatedly saying ⁠he wanted to discuss his selections rather than Ronaldo.

“All my decisions were made with the team in mind. As a manager, I have always defended what was best for the team. I am at peace with ⁠my decision,” Jesus said, insisting there were no hard feelings.

He said Ronaldo remained in his plans until Thursday’s announcement.

“I found out ⁠when we all did,” Jesus said. “Until then, I knew ⁠nothing about it. He was playing, he was scoring goals; he was one of the players on my squad list.”

Jesus said he had not subsequently contacted Ronaldo.

Proenca, meanwhile, said he, Jesus and everyone at the federation ‌respected Ronaldo’s decision, praising his leadership and influence on generations of Portuguese players.

“The best way to honour and celebrate him is to honour his boundless ambition. To always play ‌to ‌win. To never be afraid of being the best in the world,” he said.

“Thank you for everything, captain. This is and always will be your home.”
