articles.title: 6 Landing Spots for Ivan Miroshnichenko Amid NHL Trade Rumors
articles.summary: As it turns out, Nikita Kucherov isn't the only Russian winger looking for a trade. Washington Capitals forward Ivan Miroshnichenko (and his agent Dan Milstein, who is coincidentally also Kucherov's agent) has been granted permission by the Capitals to find a trade for the young forward.
articles.body:
As it turns out, Nikita Kucherov isn't the only Russian winger looking for a trade. Washington Capitals forward Ivan Miroshnichenko (and his agent Dan Milstein, who is coincidentally also Kucherov's agent) has been granted permission by the Capitals to find a trade for the young forward.

As Milstein told Daily Faceoff , the biggest issue with Miroshnichenko and the Capitals is that Washington has too many forwards. The 22-year-old, who was a first-round pick by the Caps in 2022, doesn't have much of a path to playing games.

This season, Miroshnichenko has played in three games and has a goal. He split the previous three seasons between Washington and the AHL in Hershey. If the Caps tried to send him back to the AHL, he'd have to clear waivers, and that's unlikely.

Elliotte Friedman said the Capitals would like to get at least a first-round pick for Miroshnichenko, and while sooner would be better, he also wants to be in the right situation. We'll take a look at some of the discussed locations and theorize others for ourselves.

If there are any teams that make sense to add a young, scoring winger, the Canucks belong at the top of the list.

Vancouver was one of the worst teams in the NHL last season, and they're not faring any better this season with three wins in their first 18 games. While they're scoring goals, they're also bleeding goals against, so they have many needs, but adding the 22-year-old winger would certainly give them someone else to build on, to go with Jonathan Lekkerimäki, Marco Rossi and Liam Öhgren.

While Vancouver does have first-round picks to work with, given their record and likelihood of improvement this season, giving one up for Miroshnichenko seems unlikely, but with two second-round picks in the next draft, that could be a way to bridge the gap with Washington.

The Kings haven't lit up the NHL to start the season, and one look at their roster shows they could use some younger scoring help. Acquiring Ivan Miroshnichenko would certainly help address that.

David Pagnotta of The Fourth Period has mentioned L.A. as a team that could be in the hunt for Miroshnichenko, and given that 41-year-old Corey Perry is currently in their top six forward group, why not, right?

In truth, the Kings are still without Kevin Fiala, Mats Zuccarello and Alex Turcotte, so their forward group is being stretched badly, and they've had to press guys like Kenny Connors, Martin Chromiak and Andre Lee into action out of the AHL. Miroshnichenko would deepen their group and give them another winger with high upside.

If the cost is, indeed, a first to acquire Miroshnichenko, GM Ken Holland has been bold like that in the past, although he'd probably like to see his team a bit higher in the standings and with playoffs in mind before giving up a first.

Although the bar has been set low for the Flames this season, they've been, ahem, hot of late, going 6-3-1 in their last 10 games and improving their lot in life. Recent success aside, Calgary could still use some help, and adding Ivan Miroshnichenko would improve their lineup and maybe allow them to keep good times going.

Miroshnichenko would be a fit with the Flames given their youth movement on the blue line with Simon Nemec and Zayne Parekh and the chance to blend in with Yegor Sharangovich and Matt Coronato up front.

While giving up a first-round pick is probably not in Calgary's best interests, hot play or not, they've got a pair of second-round picks available to them this year, as well as other young players that perhaps the Capitals would like in a long-term development situation.

Full marks to the Kraken, who have started off this season well and who have shown they're willing to make a deal, too. They traded their own prospect, Shane Wright, to Nashville for Matthew Wood, and with Ivan Miroshnichenko out there, perhaps Seattle would like to add yet another team's past first-round pick to the roster.

Miroshnichenko joining up with Wood, Kaapo Kakko and Mackie Samoskevich, as well as their own top guy Matty Beniers, would create a really interesting forward group, one that's shown some fight in them already this season. Given Seattle's need to get back to the playoffs, adding more firepower would be a good idea in the West.

What's more, Seattle has two first-round picks in the upcoming draft, with their own as well as the Tampa Bay Lightning's (a top-10 protected conditional pick). If the Caps wanted to move Miroshnichenko out west and get a piece of an Eastern Conference rival, sending him to the Kraken gives them the opportunity to do that.

This season could not be going worse for the Chicago Blackhawks. They're losing games, one of their big offseason additions is out injured (Bo Byram), and they're playing the kind of hockey that's a total drain to watch. Everything that could go wrong has, but if they wanted to stop feeling bad about themselves and add more young talent to their group, Ivan Miroshnichenko is there to be had.

Miroshnichenko would not have a problem getting regular minutes and opportunities with Chicago, and the Blackhawks are in a desperate situation where any move to add talent has to be considered.

Obviously, Chicago should think twice about meeting Washington's apparent asking price of a first-round pick and more, but after giving up the No. 4 pick to get Byram last offseason, maybe anything is possible for GM Kyle Davidson, and that would be music to the Caps' ears.

What's working in Chicago's favor? They have potentially three first-round picks in 2027 (their own, Florida's, and a conditional pick from Edmonton) to work with, and giving one up for a player they could have in the lineup immediately, as opposed to waiting years to see if they make it, would be really appealing to them.

Among the more desperate teams in the NHL, the Flyers certainly count as one of them, and after coming up short a few times in the offseason to add forward talent, the possibility of landing Ivan Miroshnichenko is something that could work for them in a couple of ways.

One, they would add another young, skilled forward to their group that already features Porter Martone and Matvei Michkov. Secondly, giving Michkov a fellow Russian to work with could help bring more out of his game and enhance Miroshnichenko's play with a new team in a new situation.

The downside to all this is that Washington almost certainly doesn't want to send Miroshnichenko to a division rival, and the only way to make that happen would be to pay a little more. Philly has picks to work with, but getting the Capitals on board for a trade would make for a really tricky negotiation.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 9 Fades & Busts: Bad times to continue for Panthers
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Matt Okada highlights the players we need to temper expectations for in Week 9.
articles.body:
Welcome to the ninth of 17 weekly articles spotlighting the fantasy fades of the week! I am your host, Matt Okada, and I'll be bringing you half a dozen potential busts each and every Friday, from now until fantasy football championships.

As a note, just because a player earns a "fade" or "bust" designation doesn't automatically mean they should be benched — it depends on the rest of your roster or the options on your waiver wire. But you can expect them to fall short of expectations (when I get them right). I include a "What to Do" section for every player to help with that.

Without further ado, here is my list for Week 9 of the 2026 season.

Over the first two weeks of the season, Bryce Young was brilliant, throwing for three touchdowns and hitting 24+ fantasy points in both games. Then, he suffered a minor knee injury in Week 3, which he has played through with a brace, limiting his mobility in the pocket. He hasn't thrown three touchdowns in any of Carolina's six contests since, clocking in at just seven TDs and four interceptions over that span.

In the meantime, the Panthers' offensive line has been ravaged by injuries and, in combination, these factors have led to a severe drop-off in fantasy production for Young. He's been pressured on 50% of his dropbacks over the last two weeks and has logged a 35.4 passer rating and 20% success rate against that pressure. Largely as a result, he's averaged just 9.39 fantasy points per game in those two outings.

Now, he draws a matchup with a Broncos defense sporting the league's fourth-highest pressure rate (40.3%) and second-highest quick pressure rate (21.7%), per Next Gen Stats, both of which have increased in recent weeks. Young is likely to be in trouble early and often in this game and is staring down the barrel of another fantasy dud.

What to do ❓ Young is well outside QB1 range and is honestly closer to the back of QB2 range this week. I'd much prefer a streamer like Tyler Shough, Malik Willis, Kirk Cousins or even Michael Penix Jr.

Ollie Gordon II has been shockingly good for fantasy since taking over for De'Von Achane several weeks ago. Most of the fantasy community couldn't even decide whether he'd get the starting job, and he's proceeded to average 18.8 touches per game since the Week 3 takeover and score 13+ fantasy points in four of those five contests. However, I'm pumping the brakes for Week 9.

Coming off his first dud — 6.9 points against the tough Patriots run defense — Gordon has an even tougher matchup in the Lions. Detroit is a massive pass-funnel opponent, meaning that it encourages offenses to throw — allowing a league-high 298.7 yards per game on a league-high 41 attempts per game — rather than run (where it's bottom-10 in YPG and attempts per game allowed). As a result, it's allowing the fourth-fewest fantasy points per game to running backs. And unfortunately, Gordon has essentially zero role in the Miami passing attack. If he's lucky enough to see a goal-line carry or two, Gordon could score a touchdown and eke out a decent fantasy day, but it feels far more likely that he has another medium-volume, low-efficiency day and ends up in single-digit fantasy points once again.

What to do ❓ Gordon isn't an absolute must-sit, especially given the shallow nature of the position. But he's a low-end RB2 at best and I'd definitely lower expectations and avoid him in DFS.

Speaking of the Lions' run defense, they turned Jordan Mason into an absolute dud last week, with just 20 rushing yards on eight carries for 2.0 fantasy points. That brings his total since returning from injury in Week 7 to 88 yards on 23 carries (3.8 per carry) with zero catches and zero touchdowns. Fantasy managers who waited on his return are justifiably frustrated but might see a glimmer of hope in the "green" Bills matchup here in Week 9.

Buffalo has been a good matchup for running backs because its allowed the third-most receiving fantasy points per game, at 11.0, behind only the Dolphins and 49ers. In rushing fantasy points, its much closer to the middle of the pack, and Mason is only guaranteed to see a portion of that production with Aaron Jones Sr. still involved. The Vikings offense has been extremely lackluster all season and they're an underdog against the Bills in what figures to be a relatively low-scoring affair. None of this bodes well for the run-only half of Minnesota's RBBC, so Mason is better suited on the bench until a better opportunity arises ... if ever.

What to do ❓ Mason is well outside RB2 range and I wouldn't even consider him a promising FLEX. You're better off starting committee-backs like Zach Charbonnet or Blake Corum, as they should have better chances at scoring.

Remember everything I said about Bryce Young, the Panthers' O-line and the mess that pressure has created for this passing attack lately? All of that trickles down in a very discouraging way for early breakout candidate, Jalen Coker. He has just three catches on 10 targets all season when Young is pressured and just three catches for 45 yards during this particularly troubling downturn the past two weeks. He had a brilliant game against the Eagles three weeks ago, but Philly is currently the best matchup for wide receivers, so we have to take that 97-yard game with a grain of salt. And it makes sense that pressure and Coker don't get along: he's averaged 11.2 air yards per target and 20.5% of his targets have come on deep passes this season (nearly twice as high as the rate for Tetairoa McMillan).

Meanwhile, Denver has allowed the fifth-fewest fantasy points to wide receivers and the fourth-fewest yards per target on downfield throws (10+ air yards). Just as Young is a fade, Coker is a complementary fade for all the same reasons. I like his upside down the stretch if Young and the O-line can get healthy, but he's a very risky play in the meantime.

What to do ❓ Coker is outside WR2 range and while he's a playable FLEX in a pinch, I'd rather go with a lesser name in a better situation, like Keenan Allen or Stefon Diggs.

It seems like there's a bit of growing optimism about Jaylen Waddle in the fantasy community ... but I'm not entirely sure why. Sure, he caught a touchdown in Week 8 against the Chiefs ... just his second of the year, by the way. He also finished that game with three catches for 39 yards, marking his sixth-straight game with fewer than six catches and fewer than 50 receiving yards. His only truly impressive outing all season came back in Week 2 against the Jaguars — who have proven to be a major pass-funnel defense — when he saw eight catches for 138 yards on 10 targets. But Waddle had 138 receiving yards in his other six games combined entering Week 8 and is averaging just 39.4 per game on the season, even when including that aberration of an outing against Jacksonville.

He's averaging the fourth-fewest yards per target (6.2) among all wideouts with 50+ targets and doesn't have a game over 14 fantasy points in the last six weeks. All told, his floor and ceiling are concerningly low and I see little reason for optimism against the Panthers — even with injuries to their starting cornerbacks — given how spotty and inefficient Waddle's usage has been.

What to do ❓ Waddle falls a couple spots behind Coker in my rankings, so we can apply the same logic for him in Week 9 — WR3 at best, iffy FLEX play, would rather go with Allen or Diggs.

This pains me, as I am a huge Dalton Kincaid fan, and there are a lot of reasons to believe in him rest-of-season — like his position-leading 2.7 yards per route run and his robust-for-a-tight-end air yards share (19.7%). But the Minnesota Vikings are terrifying. They've allowed a league-low 5.5 fantasy points per game to tight ends and have held every single TE they've faced to single-digit fantasy points. Tucker Kraft set the current high-water mark at just 8.0 points, while Sam LaPorta (5.0), Juwan Johnson (3.6), Colston Loveland (0.8) and others have been complete duds in this matchup.

On average, they've surrendered just 3.1 catches for 39.0 yards per game to the position, and have yet to allow a touchdown to a tight end all season. Sitting Kincaid won't be easy, especially given the shallow nature of the position, but it might be necessary given the heavily reduced ceiling against Minnesota.

What to do ❓ Try to find a streamer in redraft if you can, a la T.J. Hockenson, Kyle Pitts Sr., or even Brenton Strange, rather than playing Kincaid against this defense. And stay away in DFS.

articles.title: Worcestershire trio aim to make more Cup magic
articles.summary: Worcester City, Alvechurch and Kidderminster have all enjoyed magic moments in the FA Cup and want to create new ones in this season's first round.
articles.body:
It's now 55 seasons since non-league Hereford United's 2-1 fourth-round replay win over top-flight Newcastle United entered English football folklore as arguably the greatest FA Cup shock of all time.

Elsewhere in the Midlands, though, there have been many other upsets and moments of cup magic too.

Telford United (in 1984) and Kidderminster Harriers (in 1994) both made it to the fifth round, and Worcestershire village side Alvechurch hold a record they will keep forever - unless the rules are changed again - after taking four replays to see off Oxford City in a qualifying round tie in 1971.

Worcester City were involved in a record-breaking penalty shootout against Scunthorpe in 2014 - the same year they famously beat Coventry City.

But, while the memory of that day at Hereford - Ronnie Radford et al - surpasses all other memories, across the Worcestershire border, it perhaps still irks a bit.

Accompanied by fallen 1970s non-league stars Stafford Rangers, Worcestershire clubs make up three of the four non-EFL Midlands sides to have made it through to the first round proper - the Harriers plus seventh-tier duo Alvechurch and Worcester, who all face EFL clubs. How will they fare this time?

5th in League One v 6th in Southern League Premier Central (Tier 7)

On paper, it looks a very tall order for Alvechurch. But not every non-league club has got an FA Cup pedigree like the Church's manager Kyle Storer.

The former Bedworth United, Tamworth, Hinckley United, Atherstone Town, Nuneaton Town, Kiddy Harriers, Wrexham, Cheltenham Town, Solihull Moors, Nuneaton Borough, AFC Telford United, Kettering Town and Alvechurch player is not just a walking advert for Midlands non-league football, he has got plenty of FA Cup "previous" to be taken into consideration.

"I've been very fortunate," Storer told BBC Midlands Today.

"I got to the fourth round with Kiddy Harriers, when we played at Sunderland in front of 40,000. And that was having beaten Peterborough over two games with a team that had Joe Lolley, Marvin Johnson and Chey Dunkley."

"And, when I was at Tamworth, we won at Bournemouth [ Storer actually scored the winner] , then took Stoke to a replay. And we got Norwich at home in third round the following year."

Dion Dublin and Darren Huckerby both netted twice in a 4-1 win but Storer had the last word by getting one back. "It was voted goal of the round too," he grins.

"I've had some amazing FA Cup runs but let's hope we can go and create another day to remember. Let's hope we can cause some damage.

"in terms of football prospects, it's a tough one. They're flying, aren't they? But, in financial terms, then it's amazing."

23rd in League Two v 17th in Southern League Premier Central (Tier7)

For the younger generations, ask any Worcester City fan what the FA Cup means to them and they will bring up the 2013-14 season.

City caused "Pandemonium at the Ricoh", as BBC Hereford & Worcester freelance reporter Dan Johnson excitedly put it, when they beat then League One side Coventry.

Then came that 14-13 spotkicks defeat by Scunthorpe United in that astonishing, record-breaking 30-penalty shootout.

City also made the first round the following season when, despite having Troy Deeney's brother Ellis in the side, they were well beaten 3-0 at Bramall Lane by Sheffield United .

This is their first appearance in the first round proper since then.

But, for the result that still counts as City's biggest FA Cup scalp, you have to go way back to January 1959 - and the arrival of Liverpool at their old St George's Lane home.

It was 11 months before the great Bill Shankly arrived at Liverpool to create the legendary 'Mighty Red' machine which became kings of English football and conquered all of Europe in the 1960s, 70s and 80s.

At the time, they were still in Division Two - and not promoted until 1962 after eight years in the second tier - but it's a memory that then schoolboy, Roger King, will ever forget.

"The game should have been on the Saturday but it was postponed," Roger told BBC Midlands Today. "It was quite icy.

"I was at school then, Christopher Whitehead Secondary Modern. The game was rearranged for the following Wednesday afternoon and the only way you could attend was to get the ticket signed by my father, to take the headmaster and he gave you permission to have the afternoon off.

"I can't remember much of the game but I do remember the crowd. We got to the ground at one o'clock and didn't get in until gone two o'clock. St George's Lane was just a residential street and it was thronged with thousands.

"A lot of people talk about Hereford and their notable win, but we'll never forget our win over Liverpool."

Can City cause another upset on Saturday? Well, Danny Cowley's Colchester have not won since a 1-0 victory over Rochdale on 29 August - 12 games ago - and have slipped to 23rd in League Two.

It might not be Liverpool or Coventry, but it would be another significant scalp for Worcester. And it was in Essex 68 years ago that their Cup heroics all began, when they drew 0-0 with Chelmsford and beat them in a first-round replay.

Kidderminster Harriers v Doncaster Rovers

13th in National League v 20th in League One

After early exits in the qualifying rounds over the last two seasons, when they were a sixth-tier side, regular cup fighters Kidderminster Harriers make ther first appearance in round one since losing 2-1 at home to Fleetwood in 2023 .

After promotion in May, Harriers made a great start back in the fifth tier under new manager Paul Wotton. But they have now not won in eight league games - their only victory in that time coming at home to fellow Midlanders Solihull Moors in the fourth qualifying round.

Now they face Grant McCann's Doncaster, who have themselves won just three league games so far this season.

"You always want to win your next game," Wotton told BBC Hereford & Worcester. "And we're at home. And there's no pressure on us.

"I know the manager well. I've played against him many times and I've been assistant manager when he's been the manager on the opposite bench.

"We're full time, so we'll have no excuses fitness-wise but they're two leagues higher than us.

"It's still a big jump for us. We're a million miles from League One.

"But don't let anyone ever tell you can't do anything. We'll be as committed as we possibly can."

articles.title: Central Falls, Classical head to the D-II boys soccer championship
articles.summary: Here's how Central Falls and Classical reached the D-II boys soccer championship.
articles.body:
JOHNSTON — Central Falls might have that magic. And Classical survived on grit.

The Warriors were relentless for 80 minutes against Mt. Hope to continue their unexpected playoff run. A pair of goals from Daniel Rios Aceituno paced a 3-1 comeback in a Division II semifinal victory over the Huskies.

Peter Breen closed out an unending night between Classical vs. Central in the second semifinal. The senior's penalty kick lifted the Purple to a 0-0 (6-5) victory after eight penalty rounds on a breezy, Nov. 5 night at Johnston High School.

The eighth-ranked Huskies and third-ranked Purple advance to the championship at Rhode Island College on Sunday at 2:30 p.m.

It's the first title appearance for Central Falls, who are looking for their fifth championship overall, since it won a D-III crown in 2005. Classical advances to a title round for the first time since 2014 when it won a D-II championship. Central Falls won the season meeting against Classical, 4-1, in Providence in mid-September.

"I told the team to keep our head up," Rios Aceituno said. "Just keep it up and keep pushing. We've been working hard in practice every day."

"Right before I take that kick, I know what I'm going to do," Breen said. "I feel calm. If the goalie guesses right, he guesses. But if he doesn't, that's awesome and we're in the championship on Sunday."

Read on below for more on the D-II boys soccer semifinals.

The Warriors dominated possession in the first half against No. 4 Mt. Hope but trailed at halftime after a clinical set-piece header from Gavin Avila in the 17th minute. After turning back No. 1 Smithfield in penalty kicks in the quarterfinals, the upset kings still had plenty of fuel for the final 40 minutes.

Kevin Ramos Pedroza provided the first cross that Rios Aceituno cleaned up with a header to the left corner with 27 minutes left. Second-chance opportunities were the Warriors' best scoring looks against Mt. Hope keeper Cole Tavares. The senior stood on his head, but Central Falls broke through and was onto the championship from there.

"We just told [each other] that we have to stay calm," Oscar Veliz Catalan said. "It doesn't matter what the scoreboard is, we just have to keep our head up. It doesn't matter if it's 2-0. Just keep our head up."

Rios Aceituno provided the helper on the second goal with a tough angle to the short post before Veliz Catalan buried for the go-ahead goal with 8:03 left. Rios Aceituno added the insurance with five minutes left.

"We came from last season, we came from not winning a game [in D-I]," Veliz Catalan said. "We came [into the year] with a good mindset, and I feel like this year really means a lot."

Goalie Senai Zerit knew penalty kicks were coming early into the second half and everyone at Johnston knew they were in for a long night. The stadium lights were on a timer to shut off at 10 p.m. and that deadline was even pushed back twice.

Zerit and Breen made sure a third extension wasn't needed. Zerit made his second save of the shootout before Breen delivered the winner. Celebration ensued at the 15-yard line as Classical denied Central a third straight penalty-shootout win in these playoffs.

"It's just a lot of emotions," Zerit said. "At the beginning of the penalty shootout, I'm just trying to stay calm and just stay confident and not let the doubt come into my mind.

"I knew when there was 30 minutes left in the second half [penalty kicks were coming]. We weren't really breaking through, it was really a stalemate because Central wasn't really attacking a lot. They were kind of sitting back and defending because they've already won two shootouts in the past. I think they were really pushing for the shootout, thinking they could take it."

Both teams moved down to the state's second league this year after finishing at the bottom of the D-I table. The Purple finished this season with their first winning record since 2019.

"This feels pretty great," Breen said. "We have not had a winning record in a long time. … We've lost a lot in the last years, so it just feels crazy."

articles.title: Doc Rivers hits Heat when they are down, questions Giannis’ IQ
articles.summary: Again out of coaching and back in the media realm, Doc Rivers wasted little time reflecting on Giannis Antetokounmpo and what went wrong during their time to...
articles.body:
Again out of coaching and back in the media realm, Doc Rivers wasted little time reflecting on Giannis Antetokounmpo and what went wrong during their time together with the Milwaukee Bucks.

Speaking on Bill Simmons' podcast , Rivers, now an NBA analyst, addressed last season's turmoil in Milwaukee that preceded Antetokounmpo's offseason trade to the Heat, while also questioning Antetokounmpo's playing style and fit with the Heat.

"Giannis wanted out, but he was a Buck. And he didn't want to be the bad guy," Rivers said on the podcast of the unease within the organization that preceded the Bucks relenting and dealing their 10-time All-Star. "He wanted (management) and those guys to say, 'We're trading you,' instead of him asking for a trade. To me, that was the game that was being played."

By season's end, Rivers was on the way out in Milwaukee, with Antetokounmpo being held out in order to help the Bucks' draft odds, in what had grown into a contentious relationship

During the podcast, River questioned Antetokounmpo's leadership.

"Giannis needed to just give himself to the team, not to anyone else," Rivers said. "I liked Giannis a lot. I liked him more as a dude. He's interesting. He's not easy. He's not easy because he plays at this crazy downhill pace. He's really a difficult guy."

That's when Rivers questioned a playing style that the Heat are attempting to integrate amid their 3-6 start.

"He has this great passing ability, but he doesn't necessarily have this super IQ at the same time," Rivers said. "It's really a strange thing, and he really has one way: downhill, force, force. Every play, he wants to force it."

Rivers added, "I wish he learned how to execute better. He's one of those guys … that have never needed to execute because they can do it on their own. But that doesn't help the team.

"And I told Giannis this, the thing he needs to still learn is the value of execution. How important it is when you're in practice and shootarounds to lock in on execution."

Rivers said he expects Heat coach Erik Spoelstra to make it work.

"And now he has a coach who is as good as there is in execution," Rivers said

Antetokounmpo was acquired in the deal that had the Heat sending out Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakucionis and draft capital.

Antetokounmpo, who is dealing with a wrist issue, did not speak after Thursday night's loss to the Golden State Warriors at Chase Center, with the Heat now idle until Sunday's game against the Sacramento Kings, the fourth stop on the team's five-game western swing.

articles.title: Soccer Saturday: 25 things to know about Section 2's 11 regional contenders
articles.summary: Eleven Section 2 boys' and girls' soccer teams will suit up for regional finals, chasing berths in the state final four.
articles.body:
The road to the state semifinals runs through Saturday.

Eleven Section 2 boys' and girls' soccer teams will suit up for regional finals, chasing berths in the state final four. Saturday features six boys' and five girls' matches, nine of which will take place at sites across the Capital Region.

Class AA: Bethlehem vs. Section 3's Watertown, 2 p.m. at Waterford-Halfmoon

Class B: Schuylerville vs. Section 7's Saranac, 2 p.m. at La Salle

Class D: Northville vs. Section 4's Edmeston Central, 3 p.m. at Chenango Valley

Class AAA: Shaker vs. Section 3's C-NS, 4:30 p.m. at Waterford-Halfmoon

Class A: Averill Park vs. Section 7's Peru, 4:30 p.m. at La Salle

Class C: Greenville vs. Section 7's Northern Adirondack, 5:30 p.m. at Northeastern Clinton

Class A: Averill Park vs. Section 7's Beekmantown, noon at Niskayuna

Class B: Schuylerville vs. Section 7's AuSable Valley, noon at Stillwater

Class AAA: Shenendehowa vs. Section 3's Cicero-North Syracuse, 2:30 p.m. at Niskayuna

Class AA: Bethlehem vs. Section 3's Fayetteville-Manlius, 2:30 p.m. at Stillwater

Class C: Stillwater vs. Section 1's North Salem, 5 p.m. at Niskayuna

From top-ranked clashes to underdogs looking to make history, here are 25 things to know before Saturday's action gets underway.

All three large-school champions in Section 2 girls' soccer came from the Suburban Council: Shenendehowa (Class AAA), Bethlehem (Class AA) and Averill Park (Class A).

The Bethlehem boys' soccer team will play Section 3's Watertown in a Class AA state regional on Saturday at 2 p.m. at Waterford-Halfmoon, a matchup that pits the state's top-ranked Class AA teams against each other. Watertown is ranked No. 1, while Bethlehem is No. 2 in the state. Bethlehem began the season ranked ninth, then moved to No. 1 on Oct. 6 before settling at No. 2 for the rest of the season.

The Shaker boys' soccer team lost its first three games of the season before going on an eight-game winning streak. The Blue Bison (13-5), ranked No. 6 in the state, bring a four-game winning streak into Saturday's state regional against the state's 12th-ranked team, Cicero-North Syracuse of Section 3.

4. Averill Park girls' soccer is in the state playoffs despite going winless in Suburban Council play against exclusively Class AAA and AA teams. Including the postseason, Averill Park is 4-0 against Class A opponents.

5. Stillwater girls' soccer is still alive in its quest to win back-to-back Class C state championships. The last Section 2 team to repeat at states was Waterford-Halfmoon, which won the Class C title in 2022 and shared it with Mount Academy in 2023.

The Bethlehem boys' soccer team is the only Section 2 team still undefeated and competing. The Eagles (15-0-3) are one of 10 undefeated boys' teams across all classes in the NYSPHAA field. Their opponent on Saturday is Watertown, which is also undefeated at 19-0-0.

Four Section 2 schools sent teams to the state playoffs for both boys' and girls' soccer: Bethlehem

(Class AA), Averill Park (Class A), Schuylerville

(Class D). Seven of those teams play Saturday, while Northville girls' soccer was eliminated in a sub-regional game earlier this week.

Sami Terra scored a hat trick to lift the Shaker boys' soccer team to a 3-1 win over Class AAA defending co-champion Guilderland in the sectional final. The senior has returned from an injury to score 17 goals this season for the Blue Bison.

9. Bethlehem girls' soccer is back in the state tournament for the first time since 2019. That season, the Eagles reached the state quarterfinals with current U.S. women's national team player Claire Hutton playing a starring role as an eighth grader.

The Averill Park boys' soccer team (8-9-2) has lost only once in its past seven games, a 2-1 setback to Class AAA champion Shaker. The Golden Knights finished 2-9-1 in Suburban Council play, but defeated Hudson Falls, Cohoes and Schalmont in the playoffs, outscoring them 15-3 to claim their first sectional title since 2021.

The Northville boys' soccer team defeated Hartford 5-0 to claim its third consecutive Class D title. The Falcons (18-1) have won eight straight games, outscoring opponents 59-0 over that span and allowing only five goals all season. Northville's lone loss this season came against the No. 1 Class D team in the state, Chazy, in early October.

It's been an immediate success for Bethlehem girls' soccer coach Scott Geis. He has the Eagles in the state playoffs in his first year as varsity coach.

Two first-year Section 2 boys' soccer coaches have led their teams to the state regionals. Greenville's boys' soccer team is led by head coach Jared McAneny, the uncle of Spartans' star Isaac McAneny. The Averill Park boys' soccer team is led by coach Dylan Martin.

The Black Horses are on the rise. Schuylerville girls' soccer had never reached a Section 2 final before last year. Now, they've been to two championship games in a row, and this year they unseated defending champion Mechanicville to get into the state tournament.

How about this high-powered rematch in Class AAA? Shenendehowa girls' soccer is the No. 1 team in the latest state rankings. The Mustangs face the No. 2 team, Section 3's Cicero-North Syracuse, in Saturday's regional final. The two teams met in early October, with Shen winning 3-0.

The Greenville boys' soccer team (16-3-1) won the Section 2 Class B title last season by defeating Mechanicville, then moved to Class C before this season began. At 6-0-1, the No. 2-ranked Spartans are unbeaten against Class C teams this season. Greenville beat defending champion Maple Hill 1-0 in overtime on a goal by Isaac McAneny and earned a sub-regional win over the state's sixth-ranked team, Burke Catholic, from Section 9.

Brittany Tetlack is powering a dangerous attack for Shenendehowa girls' soccer . The junior striker scored a hat trick in the Mustangs' sectional final win over Guilderland and has 24 goals this season.

18. Northville boys' soccer goalkeeper Joey Capobianco earned his 16th shutout of the season in the Falcons' 5-0 Section 2 Class D final over Hartford, breaking the Northville school record for most shutouts in a season.

19. Stillwater girls' soccer is on a roll. Since losing to Mechanicville in late September, the defending Class C state champions have won 13 consecutive games and outscored its opposition 67-3.

After losing to Broadalbin-Perth 1-0 in last year's sectional tournament, the Schuylerville boys' soccer team (13-3-2) beat the Patriots 1-0 in this year's Class B final, with Colden Harrison's golden goal in overtime. The win marked Schuylerville's first sectional title since 2019.

Teagan DeLair has been at the center of the late-season surge for Averill Park girls' soccer . The junior midfielder had two-goal games in both the Section 2 semifinals against Ravena-Coeymans-Selkirk and the championship game against Schalmont.

Of the six Section 2 boys' soccer teams that advanced to the state regionals on Saturday, only Shaker

have reached a state final four. Shaker was the state runner-up in 2024, while Northville was the state champion in 1988, a state co-champion in 1995, and a state runner-up in 2009 and 2024.

23. Shenendehowa girls' soccer is seeking its first state title in 22 years. The Mustangs most recently reached a state final in 2021, falling 3-0 to Massapequa in the Class AA final.

A tough defense to crack. Schuylerville girls' soccer has allowed just 15 goals all season, and hasn't allowed an opponent to score since the playoffs started. The Black Horses' Class B playoff wins over Fonda-Fultonville, Cairo-Durham, Broadalbin-Perth and Mechanicville came by a combined score of 13-0.

The Greenville boys' soccer team was one of two Section 2 teams to play in a sub-regional on Wednesday, with Class D at-large Hartford the other. articles.title: What the Chiefs are saying about the Jets
articles.summary: Kansas City’s coaching staff previewed New York at the podium this week.
articles.body:
In Week 9, the Kansas City Chiefs will host the New York Jets near the midpoint of the 2026 regular season. The game at Arrowhead Stadium will feature a coaching matchup of second-year head coach Aaron Glenn and Chiefs head coach Andy Reid in his 28th season.

At the podium Wednesday, Reid looked forward to the matchup with New York by describing the team Kansas City hasn't faced in three years. The Chiefs won a road game on "Sunday Night Football" 23-20 in Week 4 of the 2023 season.

"They're very physical on both sides of the ball," Reid said. "Scoring a lot of points on the offensive side, and their defense – they've got a lot of different looks that they're going to present. Solid veteran players that do a nice job for them."

Glenn, a former NFL cornerback and Detroit Lions defensive coordinator, is organizing a unit that just allowed 38 points to the Las Vegas Raiders at home last week. However, this season, New York ranks 11th in total yards allowed per game (318) and allows the fifth-lowest rate of passing yards per game (194).

"They've got some good veteran guys, whether it's the safeties, the linebackers. You're not going to have things that are botched up," Reid shared. "They do a good job of making sure they can adjust to most things and do it accurately. Then they've got some guys on the front that are good football players, big guys. They're good players. They've got some good speed on the outside."

Whether it's linebacker Demario Davis or safety Minkah Fitzpatrick, the Jets made sure to bring in veterans to lead Glenn's group this season. Chiefs offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy pointed out the style of defense Glenn has instilled.

"They play extremely hard," Bieniemy pointed out. "They play fast and A.G.,obviously, they haven't had the best of luck, but when you turn that tape on, they get your attention."

On the flip side, the Chiefs' defense will face a hot Jets offense. They have scored 58 points over the last two weeks, and first-round rookies in wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. and tight end Kenyon Sadiq have had big games around No. 1 wide receiver Garrett Wilson.

With Wilson in concussion protocol this week, Chiefs defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo is still ready to defend downfield passes from veteran quarterback Geno Smith, who was once his quarterback when he was defensive coordinator and interim head coach of the New York Giants in 2017.

Smith was also the quarterback for the Raiders when Kansas City pitched a 31-0 shutout with just four first downs allowed in Week 7 last year.

"I've always had a lot of respect for Geno," Spags said. "I've always had a great deal of respect for how smart he is and his rocket arm; he has a really strong arm. I put like three clips on yesterday of him from one side of the field throwing all the way [to the other], an out cut, deep to a number of different receivers. You know how talented and young they are, and they can all run that route. So we're alerted to what kind of quarterback we're dealing with."

Spagnuolo then alluded to the Jets' league-leading six players with 100-yard games this season, including running back Braelon Allen, who has stepped in since a groin injury to starter Breece Hall; Hall is expected to play on Sunday afternoon, but both backs look like threats to the coach.

"Allen has had four really good games, and it feels like they want to feature the running back no matter who's back there," Spagnuolo pointed out. "I think they're a little bit different, and yet I think they both run the scheme really well."

I think he looks Derrick Henry-ish to me sometimes," Spags described Allen. "He's a big guy. So, we've got to be on point tackling."

It will all start with run defense, where Kansas City ranks eighth in rushing yards allowed per game (96) and third in yards per rushing attempt (3.5). The Seahawks ran for 153 yards a couple of weeks ago, but no other opponent has hit 120 or more yards against the Chiefs on the ground this season.

articles.title: How Patrick Graham fixed the disconnect in the Steelers' defense
articles.summary: Linebacker Patrick Queen and the Steelers defense have fully bought into Patrick Graham's coaching philosophy during an impressive 6-2 start.
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers enter their bye week riding impressive midseason momentum, and while much of the chatter centers on the offense, the steady transformation of the defense remains the team's true backbone. Central to this defensive resurgence is new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham, whose approach has cultivated a rare level of trust across all three levels of the unit.

On the " Locked on Steelers " podcast, host Christopher Carter and guest Jenna Harner discussed how much this defense has improved through the first 8 games.

Unlike previous seasons, where operational friction between players and even staff required head coach-level intervention, Graham has successfully eliminated structural disconnects. By directly coaching the front seven, the defensive line and linebackers, while trusting secondary coaches Joe Witt, Jr. and Jason Simmons to manage the defensive backfield, Graham has established an environment of total buy-in.

"This is a group and a coordinator that is really seeing the trust in each other," Harner observed, noting how intangible chemistry translates into physical output. "Patrick Queen is talking about that. He's saying he's some of the happiest he's been in Pittsburgh because of the way that they're all just trusting each other and being behind each other."

Queen's perspective highlights a dramatic shift. The linebacker's previous frustration with defensive calls was apparent, but Graham's arrival eliminated the need for mid-season mediation. Insiders emphasize that Graham's strength lies in his ability to connect personally with the front line.

"Patrick Graham, to give him credit, he's connected with every layer of the defense," Carter explained. "He was a guy who connected with the guys up front, D-linemen, linebackers. He loves to coach those guys, and then he trusts the guys in the secondary."

By fostering mutual respect and clear communication, Graham has elevated the defense beyond simple scheme execution. That alignment gives Pittsburgh a legitimate championship-caliber identity capable of anchoring a deep playoff run.

articles.title: TIME MACHINE: GENOA vs. AC MILAN
articles.summary: Before the international break, it was an away match against Genoa. After the home Derby, the Rossoneri were back on the road for Matchday 11 of Serie A, hea...
articles.body:
Before the international break, it was an away match against Genoa. After the home Derby, the Rossoneri were back on the road for Matchday 11 of Serie A, heading to the Stadio L. Ferraris in Genoa's Marassi district, where on December 2, 2011 , AC Milan produced a convincing 2-0 win, inspired by the brilliance of Zlatan Ibrahimović and a strong all-around team performance. This was Allegri's second season in charge, with the reigning champions still in excellent form.

It was a wintery Friday night, and Van Bommel, Pato and Abbiati were all unavailable. It was not quite an injury crisis, but hardly ideal preparation for an important, tricky fixture. The Rossoneri were coming off a dominant 4-0 win over ChievoVerona at San Siro and had not lost since the start of October, when they were lost away against Juventus, their closest rivals in the title race. It was not a straightforward evening, with play briefly interrupted by crowd trouble inside the stadium.

Ibrahimović and Nocerino proved to be a dangerous combination. Early on, the striker twice picked out the midfielder's runs, with Nocerino denied first by Rossi and then by Frey from close range. Robinho, Boateng and Nocerino all had further attempts without finding the target, before Ibra forced another save from Frey. Genoa grew into the game late in the first half: Amelia punched away a dangerous Veloso free kick, while Mesto failed to capitalize on a mix-up between Thiago Silva and Yepes in possession.

The turning point came in the 56th minute . Robinho sent Ibrahimović through, and the Swede was brought down inside the box by former AC Milan defender Kaladze , who was shown a second yellow card and sent off. Penalty: Ibrahimović made no mistake, drilling his spot kick home to give AC Milan the lead. The closing stages were more comfortable, although Robinho somehow missed from point-blank range and Rossi went close with a backheel that drifted wide. Then, in the 79th minute , AC Milan put the result beyond doubt. Boateng delivered into the box and Nocerino arrived to finish calmly from close range. 2-0 to the Rossoneri , who would ultimately fall short in their bid to retain the title at the end of the 2011/12 season.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Start 'Em Sit 'Em: Justin Boone's Week 9 lineup advice
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Justin Boone shares his top sits and starts for Week 9.
articles.body:
Justin Boone provides a weekly look at undervalued fantasy players to consider starting this week and potential busts you might want to leave on your bench.

For the rest of your lineup decisions, consult his Week 9 rankings.

It's almost surprising that Prescott is the QB11 in fantasy points per game this year, considering he went a month without a multi-touchdown game at one point. Fortunately, he's found the end zone at least twice in each of the past two weeks.

Now Prescott faces a Colts team that's circling the drain before a likely selloff at the trade deadline. In its first game after dealing Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner, Indy was dismantled 42-7 by the Jaguars. The Cowboys are 5.5-point favorites on the road with the fourth-highest implied point total on the week.

Though Dak hasn't been the most reliable fantasy option this season, you can start him confidently as a top-five QB versus the Colts.

Malik Willis vs. Lions – With the Dolphins' young receiving corps getting healthy, Willis has been heating up lately as a solid fantasy streamer who offers a high floor and high ceiling. This is setting up to be a potential ceiling game for him, against a Detroit defense giving up the most fantasy points to QBs, including multiple TDs in every outing.

C.J. Stroud at Chargers – Stroud has quietly had a very solid season and, with the Texans' struggles in the run game, you can expect the team to continue relying on his arm. The 25-year-old is tied for the fifth most fantasy points among quarterbacks over the last five weeks. Coming off the bye, Stroud should get a boost from Marvin Harrison Jr. getting more comfortable in the offense and Tank Dell seeing a rise in snaps.

Brown only finished as the RB20 in a great matchup with the Titans last week, but that would have been a top-12 fantasy back if his 20-yard touchdown catch wasn't nullified by a penalty.

The good news is that Brown continues to dominate the Bengals backfield, paying almost 70% of the snaps last week and turning them into 20 touches, 101 scrimmage yards and eight catches.

He also gets another positive matchup with the Falcons defense that's the fourth easiest matchup for fantasy running backs. Atlanta has allowed seven touchdowns to RBs over its last three games and just got decimated for over 300 rushing yards by the Buccaneers backs in Week 8.

I know it's been frustrating at times having Brown in your lineup; just don't give up now. Bigger days are within reach. If you are planning to sell him, you'll want to wait until after this game to get the most value.

Jonah Coleman at Panthers – Coleman returned from IR and immediately took control of the Broncos backfield, playing 58% of the snaps over the last two weeks and racking up 173 scrimmage yards, six receptions and a touchdown. Now, he gets a Panthers defense that's permitting the second-most fantasy points to his position. The rookie is a top-15 fantasy RB option this week.

Blake Corum at Commanders – Over the last month, the Rams offense has leaned on their backfield more with Davante Adams hitting IR. That resulted in both backs averaging top-15 fantasy stats, with Corum at RB13 and Kyren Williams at RB15. Don't be misled; Williams is still the lead back and Corum hasn't played over 50% of the snaps in any game. However, he's getting plenty of opportunity, which should continue as 5.5-point favorites over the Commanders.

Tyler Allgeier at Seahawks – While I hate the matchup, it's impossible to argue with the setup for Allgeier. Jeremiyah Love is on IR and Bam Knight is in concussion protocol. That leaves Allgeier as the last man standing in Arizona's RB room. Though you can't expect another 191-yard, five-catch, two-touchdown performance (because he's not playing the Cowboys defense), Allgeier can still be started as a volume-based low-end RB2.

Jefferson isn't a name that makes it to the Start section very often because he's such a talented player that fantasy managers don't need a reminder. However, given the state of the quarterback play in Minnesota, starting Jefferson wasn't as obvious as it had been in the past.

The veteran wideout has been held to receiving-yard totals of 55, 32, 44 and 33 in four of his last five outings and Kyler Murray wasn't finding his rhythm in Kevin O'Connell's scheme.

Murray's new hamstring injury gave the coaching staff a chance to make a change and they jumped on it, naming Carson Wentz the starter for Monday's matchup with the Bills. With Buffalo's defense still being a work in progress, Wentz and company should be able to get the Vikings' passing game back on track.

That's great news for Jefferson, who has averaged 6.4 receptions and 89.1 receiving yards during the seven games where Wentz has played at least 80% of the snaps over the last two seasons. That includes an 8-92-2 stat line from the opener this year.

This move pushed Jefferson back into the top-10 fantasy WRs and in the conversation for a spot in the top-five for as long as Wentz is under center.

George Pickens at Colts – Pickens has been playing through shoulder and hamstring injuries the last couple of weeks and his playing time has taken a slight hit because of it. Jerry Jones was very clear this week that he believes Pickens needs to be getting the ball more, so this could be the rare squeaky wheel game initiated by the owner. As it stands, Pickens is still 14th in receiving yards among wideouts, but that ranking could rise thanks to a matchup with the Colts.

Rashee Rice vs. Jets – For all the concerns about Rice before the season, he's actually performed well in every outing. Rice has at least 83 yards or a touchdown in all four of his healthy appearances, including a 7-53-1 stat line in his first game back last week, despite only playing 56% of the snaps. That number should rise in a favorable spot against the Jets defense that plays a lot of single-high coverage, which Rice excels against.

Rome Odunze vs. Buccaneers – Odunze is 20th in receiving yards, but 53rd in fantasy points scored among wideouts. The discrepancy exists due to a lack of touchdowns, with Odunze not finding the end zone yet this season. Fortunately, the offense has been regaining its form with Caleb Williams back and Odunze has posted two of his best outings this season in recent weeks, with 69 yards against the Patriots and 87 yards versus the Seahawks. Next up is a Bucs defense that's allowed five different WRs to top 85 yards in the last month.

Through the first five weeks, LaPorta was a top-five fantasy tight end against one of the easier schedules at his position. Then came a bye, followed by back-to-back matchups against the two toughest defenses against his position: the Packers and Vikings.

That led conspiracy theorists to speculate that the team was punishing LaPorta for his comments about being frustrated with contract extension talks with the organization. I'm guessing the degree of difficulty being turned up on him had more to do with it.

Thankfully, a softer matchup has arrived with the Dolphins defense giving up the third most fantasy points to tight ends. The Lions are also tied for the second-highest implied point total on the slate. This all points to a bounce-back week for LaPorta, which is why he's back in my top five.

Kyle Pitts Sr. vs. Bengals – After three straight top-12 TE finishes, Pitts finally came back down to earth with just two catches for six yards in a rainy loss to the Bucs last week. Now, he suits up for a potential shoutout in the dome against a Bengals defense that's the ninth most generous unit to tight ends.

Mike Gesicki at Falcons – You can also start the other tight end in that game, with Gesicki having a great chance to extend his touchdown streak versus Atlanta. The veteran has scored a touchdown in six of his seven outings and currently sits as the TE6 in fantasy points per game. You could do worse than streaming him in a game that's tied for the highest projected point total at 52.5.

It seems like the distant past now, but Young was the QB4 overall in fantasy points per game through the first six weeks, in part thanks to an easy early-season schedule. Life comes at you fast, though and a slew of injuries on the offensive line have completely changed the outlook for this offense. It doesn't help that their last two opponents have been much tougher, the Buccaneers and Packers, leading to a test that Young ultimately failed.

Coming off his two lowest fantasy outputs of the season, Young now has another difficult challenge ahead with the Broncos defense that got back Patrick Surtain II last week. There will be better days ahead, including the Saints matchup in Week 10, but for now, Young needs to head to your bench.

Geno Smith at Chiefs – Kansas City's defense is allowing the sixth-fewest fantasy points to quarterbacks and tends to be even more stout at home. Meanwhile, the Jets are likely to be without their top receiver Garrett Wilson, who is in concussion protocol. This isn't the spot to play Smith.

Baker Mayfield at Bears – At some point, Mayfield will begin throwing again and this could be the week, since he's facing a high-scoring Bears offense. But forgive me if I'm not interested in starting a quarterback who hasn't topped 13 fantasy points in a game this season and has only attempted 14 passes over the last two weeks.

White came through in Week 8 thanks to a touchdown, but his usage (13 touches, 47% snap share) was disappointing given the matchup with the Eagles and the fact that Jacory Croskey-Merritt is on IR.

The situation isn't getting better this week against a Rams defense that's his toughest opponent yet. Not only are they allowing the seventh-fewest fantasy points to running backs, but it's possible Myles Garrett could be activated for the game.

This all points to a risky setup for White, who will likely need another touchdown to save his fantasy day again.

Zach Charbonnet vs. Cardinals – The Seahawks are 8.5-point favorites, so the possibility of a goal-line carry is always there. However, it's tough to get overly excited about Charbonnet, who managed just 29 yards on nine touches while playing 37% of the snaps in his season debut. Rookie Jadarian Price displayed far more juice during the game and should earn more touches moving forward, while Charbonnet remains in a supporting role.

Omarion Hampton vs. Texans – Coming off the Chargers' bye, Hampton played a season-low 29.5% of the snaps. The sophomore back has only topped 56 scrimmage yards once this season. Like most of the running backs in this section, he's purely a TD-or-bust RB3.

Jordan Mason vs. Bills – Mason returned to the lineup in Week 7 with a 64% snap share and 15 carries for 68 yards. Unfortunately, just one week later, those numbers dropped to 28% of the snaps and just eight carries for 20 yards. While the matchup with the Bills is a positive one, it's hard to trust Mason until we see more from him and the Vikings offense as a whole.

Wilson finally rediscovered his ceiling with an eight-catch, 111-yard, one-touchdown performance, but it took a very friendly matchup with the Cowboys to get there.

Wilson also accomplished the feat while playing through two broken ribs, something that will continue to be a challenge this week.

It's also worth remembering that Wilson was held to 55 yards or less in three straight games before that springboard encounter with Dallas. The Seahawks defense, which is giving up the fewest fantasy points to wideouts, won't be the same kind of pushover. That makes Wilson a volatile WR3.

Jalen Coker vs. Broncos – The issues on the offensive line and the difficult matchup with the Broncos defense are more than enough reason to avoid Coker this week. He's only managed three catches over his last two outings.

Chris Godwin Jr. at Bears – Godwin hasn't topped 50 receiving yards in a game this season and hasn't reached 40 yards in his last six appearances. Injuries have simply sapped his effectiveness, and given his age, it's likely his best days are behind him.

Xavier Worthy vs. Jets – Worthy has been held to 25 yards or less in five of his seven games this season. He's also only found the end zone once all year, making him a very shaky flex option at best.

Kincaid's best performances have coincided with DJ Moore being in the lineup, which gives you hope that he can get back to being a top-10 fantasy tight end the rest of the way. Unfortunately, this week's matchup is with the Vikings defense, which is the biggest threat to tight ends by far this season.

Minnesota is allowing just 5.5 fantasy points per game, with the second-place Packers coming in at 7.0 fppg. The Vikings also haven't allowed a touchdown to a tight end and we've yet to see them give up more than 65 yards to a player at the position. Even if you look back to last year, Brian Flores' crew was the eighth-worst opponent for tight ends. If Kincaid comes through this week, it will be an outlier based on what we've seen from this defense in 2026.

Chig Okonkwo vs. Rams – After back-to-back 60-plus-yard games, Okonkwo managed just two catches for 32 yards in a tougher matchup with the Eagles last week. The Rams are the seventh most difficult opponent for fantasy tight ends, so I wouldn't get my hopes up here.

Tyler Higbee at Commanders – Higbee has been held to 22 yards, 14 yards and 14 yards over his last three outings, and it's possible Terrance Ferguson could return for this contest.

articles.title: Michigan State football fans have clear favorite for best win over U-M
articles.summary: Which MSU-U-M football game in the last 40 years was the most memorable? State Journal readers who took this week’s poll have a clear favorite.
articles.body:
EAST LANSING — What's the most memorable football game between the Michigan State Spartans and the Michigan Wolverines in the last four decades?

On the eve of the Nov. 7 night game in Ann Arbor, State Journal readers overwhelmingly agree that it was the Oct. 17, 2015 "Trouble with the snap!" game.

After U-M's Blake O'Neill fumbled the snap with 10 seconds left and UM leading 23-21, MSU's Jalen Watts-Jackson gathered the ball out of the air and returned it for a touchdown as the clock ran out. The stunned looks on the faces of U-M fans watching in the stands were captured on TV. Final score MSU 27, Michigan 23.

More than two-thirds, 69% of the votes in the online poll cast, were for the Oc. 17, 2015 game.

About 12% of the votes were for the Oct. 30, 2021 game. Kenneth Walker III, now a star in the NFL, had a career game with five touchdowns, including a game-winning score from 23 yards out with five minutes left in the fourth quarter. Final score: MSU 37, Michigan 33.

Nearly 7% voted for the Nov. 3, 2001 matchup. Sixth-ranked U-M was leading, 24-20, and the clock was ticking down as MSU was on its final drive just a few yards from the end zone. With no timeouts remaining, MSU spiked the ball to stop the clock, which seemed to stick on one second rather than running out. Using that remaining second for a final play, MSU quarterback Jeff Smoker scrambled and threw an off-balance pass that was caught by T.J. Duckett for the winning score. Final score: Michigan State 26, No. 6 Michigan 24.

Just over 5% of the votes cast were for the Oct. 13, 1990 game. U-M was ranked No. 1 in the country despite being 3-1 when it played MSU. The Wolverines drove to the north end of Michigan Stadium and scored with 6 seconds remaining but still trailed, 28-27. Then U-M went for a two-point conversion in lieu of a game-tying extra-point kick. U-M receiver Desmond Howard beat MSU cornerback Eddie Brown and was wide open as the pass came, but Brown tripped him. The ball bounced off Howard's hands, no penalty was called, and the unranked Spartans had a huge upset. Final score: MSU 28, Michigan 27.

About 3.5% of the votes were for the Oct. 9, 1999 game. Both MSU and U-M were top 10 teams, and unbeaten, when they played. MSU quarterback Bill Burke and receiver Plaxico Burress led the Spartans out to a big lead and it looked they were on their way to a blowout win. Then U-M senior Tom Brady, who didn't start the game, came in to lead two late touchdown drives. The Spartans, coached by Nick Saban, held on to win by three. Final score: MSU 34, Michigan 31.

About 3% of the votes were for the Oct. 25, 2008 game. MSU's win came more than six years after the Spartans had last held the Paul Bunyan Trophy. The Spartans hadn't won in Ann Arbor since 1990. With Mark Dantanio at the helm, MSU won on a play-action touchdown pass from Brian Hoyer to fullback Josh Rouse. Hoyer and Blair White starred, but Javon Ringer put the Spartans on his back with 194 yards on 37 carries — a couple days after tearing a knee ligament. Final score: Michigan State 35, Michigan 21.

articles.title: Global Lacrosse Games roster breakdown: Canada women
articles.summary: Canada is consistently one of the top two nations in the world in women’s lacrosse, and has been for decades. This country has produced some of the greatest...
articles.body:
Canada is consistently one of the top two nations in the world in women's lacrosse, and has been for decades. This country has produced some of the greatest lacrosse players in history, like the legendary Dana Dobbie. We are bound to see more greatness from this squad that has a No. 1 ranking in mind to chase after.

The roster Canada has put together for the Lexus Global Lacrosse Games is an exciting mixture of seasoned leaders and exploding stars. Let's break it down.

Erica Evans Annabel Child Jordan Dean Milana Zizakovic Kassidy Morris Aurora Cordingley Maggie Cuddy Nicole Perroni Megan Kinna Madalyn Baxter Kylea Dobson

This Canadian team is primed and prepped for a big tournament. They have battled to the very end against USA the last few times the rival nations have matched up in a Sixes Championship, and are likely itching to get over that hump.

Players like Erica Evans , Megan Kinna, Nicole Perroni and Aurora Cordingley have played on these big stages in a Canadian uniform before. Evans brings a decade of familiarity alone, playing with the Canadian national team since 2015. Their experience from playing for Canada for many years will bring a level of poise and comfort to the Global Lacrosse Games that's needed to thrive and win against the other top nations in the world.

Evans is coming off a championship summer with the Maryland Charm and has been an international star since she won a gold medal with the U19 Canadian team. She started off a historic run by being named to that 2015 All-World Team and has since been an All-World selection in nearly every international event she has participated in – in all disciplines: field, Sixes and box.

She is a strong lefty and dominant force in the middle of the field, sparking transition plays and coming up with big caused turnovers. Her offensive IQ is next-level; she executes two-player games seamlessly and constantly opens up scoring opportunities for herself and others. Evans will be the main all-around Canadian player to keep an eye on throughout each game.

Halsall is the type of goalkeeper who can make or break the outcome of a game. She stands tall in the crease and is a strong-handed lefty who clears the ball quickly the moment she makes a save in order to provide scoring opportunities for her offense going the other way.

She is one of the goalies who thrives in a Sixes setting due to substantial breakaway shot opportunities that result from the fast pace of games. Halsall's patience to not bite on shooters' fakes and her ability to make a last-second sprawling stop are two of her many game-altering abilities as Canada's main keeper.

In one of Canada's most recent matchups against USA in the Pan-American Sixes Championship in October, penalties stacked up toward the end of the game and allowed the Americans the chance to win. More penalties means more precious time spent with one less player on the field, which is a situation all teams try to avoid whenever possible. This is especially true in Sixes, where the momentum can swing even faster than in the full-field game because multiple goals can be scored in a matter of seconds without wasting any penalty time resetting at the draw.

Learning from these errors and working hard to avoid penalties, especially late in tight games, will be imminent to Canada's success in the Global Lacrosse Games.

Star power is no issue for Canada. From Evans to Halsall, Cordingley to Dean, Kinna to Perroni, this Canadian roster is stacked. The true question is whether their depth will be able to match up to that of the United States roster.

Every time these two countries play against one another, it's a highly anticipated contest. Rivalry games like these often come down to the wire, and the unsung heroes coming from the depths of the roster typically end up being the game-changers. This time around will be an excellent test for Canada's depth and an all-time game for us lacrosse fans to tune into.

The last time Canada won a women's gold medal was at the 2022 World Games, when it beat USA by a close score of 14-12. Since then, the USA has consistently been triumphant in international matchups, though Canada has kept the score close, staying within a one-goal margin multiple times. The final score of the 2023 World Lacrosse Super Sixes event was 8-7 in favor of the Americans, and the Canadians most recently lost a 15-14 thriller at the 2026 Pan-American Sixes Lacrosse Championship.

Can this roster break the one-goal curse when it lines up against the USA on Dec. 11? Having a taste of gold from 2022 and bringing that motivation into every international matchup definitely fuels the fire behind this Canadian team.

We'll get a chance to witness Canada's spark in action starting on Dec. 9 against the Haudenosaunee at 5:30 p.m. ET. Explore here for more information on the Lexus Global Lacrosse Games.

articles.title: Did NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani just take shot at LeBron James despite 76ers beating Knicks twice already this season?
articles.summary: Despite playing for the Philadelphia 76ers, who have already beaten the New York Knicks twice, LeBron James is reportedly living in the Big Apple, which mig...
articles.body:
Despite playing for the Philadelphia 76ers, who have already beaten the New York Knicks twice, LeBron James is reportedly living in the Big Apple, which might've been alluded to by NYC Mayor Zohran Mamdani.

As Mamdani's conversation with CNN after the midterms was ending, Jake Tapper threw in a subtle shot at the Knicks, saying, "Just one note — the Sixers have beaten the Knicks twice this season," before throwing it over to Anderson Cooper.

The quick-witted Mamdani didn't let that slide . The mayor promptly responded, "We've got the pied-à-terre [tax] coming anyway."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Could that have been a sneaky jab at James? A pied-à-terre is a secondary living space, and an annual tax on them recently took effect on July 1, 2026.

Is 76ers star LeBron James living in New York City?

Before the season, James confirmed that "multiple residences" would be in use during his time with the Sixers. He reportedly has access to a Fanatics helicopter to transport him to Philly .

LeBron's twilight years in his NBA career are going to be with the 76ers. He signed a two-year contract with a player option during the offseason.

He and the 76ers spoiled the Knicks' Opening Night festivities. The Knicks were celebrating their championship, handing out rings to the players and raising the banner into the rafters at Madison Square Garden. LeBron and Co. came in and beat New York in the season opener. They beat them again just over a week later, this time in the City of Brotherly Love.

The Sixers have a mix of young and veteran stars. Tyrese Maxey has started fast, averaging 28 points per game. VJ Edgecombe, Jaylen Brown—who also joined the team in the offseason—and Joel Embiid round out the starting five.

articles.title: Duke vs. North Texas women's basketball game falls apart. Blue Devils now playing at FAU
articles.summary: Duke women's basketball was supposed to play North Texas in San Antonio. Now, the game isn't happening. The Blue Devils will play FAU instead.
articles.body:
Duke's women's basketball team was scrambling this week to fill an unexpected hole in its schedule.

The Blue Devils were scheduled to face North Texas this Sunday, Nov. 8, at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas, in an event called "The Foundry Classic" (1 p.m. CT, ESPNU).

But on Thursday night, head coaches in the Patriot League and Metro Conference got emails from their league office that Duke was in "urgent need of a replacement game" for this Sunday, three people directly familiar with the situation told USA TODAY Sports. The emails said the Blue Devils were willing to play on the road or could pay an opponent to face them in Cameron Indoor Stadium in Durham, North Carolina.

Tickets for the North Texas game were also no longer available on Ticketmaster as of Thursday night.

On Friday morning, North Texas and Duke both confirmed in statements that the game was canceled "due to circumstances beyond the control of participating institutions." A spokesperson for North Texas told USA TODAY Sports that it will not search for a replacement opponent and play its next game on Nov. 11 against Houston Christian.

Duke will now play at Florida Atlantic on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET.

Organizers for the event did not immediately respond to USA TODAY Sports' request for comment. A spokesperson for Frost Bank Arena also did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Spokespersons for Duke and North Texas declined to elaborate on how the game fell apart.

2026 preseason All-Americans in women's college basketball from Studio IX

Duke versus North Texas was originally announced on Sept. 22, bringing Duke players and San Antonio natives Bella Flemings and Arianna Roberson home to play in front of family and friends. It was set to be the first meeting between Duke and North Texas in women's basketball.

It was also supposed to be a multi-day event, with players from Duke and North Texas participating in "The Foundry Future Summit, a 'student-centered experience" on Saturday, Nov. 7, which aimed to provide "opportunities for students to engage with college athletes beyond the basketball court." Additionally, Duke coach Kara Lawson and North Texas coach Jason Burton were supposed to be featured in "a moderated conversation at The Foundry Table."

Burton is in his fourth season as the head coach of the North Texas Mean Green and has three winning seasons under his belt there. North Texas is 1-1 this season after losing to San Diego State on Thursday.

Lawson, who is also the head coach of Team USA, is beginning her seventh season at the helm of the Blue Devils. Duke, coming off back-to-back ACC Tournament titles and a second consecutive trip to the Elite Eight, is 1-0 this season after opening the year with a win at home over Green Bay.
