articles.title: Eagles vs. Giants: 4 overlooked storylines for Sunday's NFC East game
articles.summary: A Giants' drought, Joe Milton's connection to Ken O'Brien, and Dennard Wilson's return highlight four Week 9 Eagles stories.
articles.body:
Two longtime rivals meet Sunday with plenty of familiar storylines , but this matchup has a few unusual details worth exploring. The Philadelphia Eagles join their long-time rivals, the New York Giants , and start their third quarterback of the regular season. J.J. McCarthy is making his second start for New York, and Joe Milton is preparing for his first with Philadelphia .

Milton will make that debut wearing the beloved Kelly Green uniforms, too. Raise your hand if you predicted that before the season began. An old feud puts two NFC East teams on a collision course, and as so often happens, there are plenty of storylines to talk about.

Not every interesting detail will help the Eagles win a football game. Some are simply fun pieces of history, while others add another layer to a rivalry that rarely needs extra motivation. From a quarterback connection stretching back more than three decades to a former Philadelphia assistant now calling the shots for New York's defense, here are four stories that might not dominate the headlines but deserve some attention.

Joe Milton joins Ken O'Brien in some lesser-mentioned Eagles lore

There aren't many connections between Joe Milton and former Eagles quarterback Ken O'Brien, but NBC Sports Philadelphia's Reuben Frank certainly found an interesting parallel. On his Eagle Eye podcast with Dave Zangaro , he mentioned that Milton will become the first Eagles quarterback to join the team after the beginning of the regular season and start a game since O'Brien did so in 1993.

O'Brien arrived in Philadelphia under unusual circumstances. The Eagles signed the former New York Jets quarterback on Oct. 4, 1993, after Randall Cunningham broke his leg and the team needed help at the position.

O'Brien eventually made four starts for Philadelphia that season, giving him a brief but memorable chapter in Eagles history. More than three decades later, Milton is stepping in, albeit under different circumstances, but the historical connection is an interesting footnote as he prepares to make his first start for Philadelphia. No one probably expected to mention him and O'Brien in the same breath, but here we are. Much can change during a football season.

The Giants ' long losing streak in Philadelphia

Here's one Giants fans know well. New York hasn't won a game in Philadelphia since Oct. 27, 2013. That afternoon, New York escaped with a 15-7 victory behind five field goals from kicker Josh Brown. The Giants haven't won at Lincoln Financial Field since, losing 13 consecutive games in hostile territory.

That's an extraordinary stretch for a division rival that plays a team twice per season. The Giants have had opportunities to end the drought, but Philadelphia has continued to protect its home field.

Sunday's matchup offers another chance, and New York has a chance to change the narrative. Ending that streak would be a significant statement in a rivalry that has largely belonged to the Eagles in recent years.

Former Michigan quarterbacks who played under Jim Harbaugh

Joe Milton and J.J. McCarthy never shared a Michigan Wolverines locker room, but they have more in common than their upcoming NFL matchup. Both played for Jim Harbaugh in Ann Arbor. Milton arrived first, and McCarthy followed after his exit.

Milton played for the Wolverines from 2018-20 before transferring to the Tennessee Volunteers , where he spent the 2021-23 seasons. McCarthy arrived in Ann Arbor in 2021 and helped lead Michigan to the College Football Playoff national championship following the 2023 season. He also earned Rose Bowl MVP honors after the Wolverines defeated the Alabama Crimson Tide in the semifinal.

The two quarterbacks took different paths through college, but their careers now intersect in the NFC East. McCarthy is trying to establish himself as New York's quarterback of the future, playing for Jim Harbaugh's brother, John. Milton has a chance to make an impression in Philadelphia. Neither player could have known their Michigan connection would eventually become a small part of an NFL rivalry matchup.

Giants defensive coordinator Dennard Wilson has a history with the Eagles, and it's not difficult to imagine this matchup carrying some extra significance for him. Wilson coached Philadelphia's defensive backs in 2021 and 2022, adding the title of defensive passing game coordinator during his second season. The Eagles' secondary flourished under his watch, allowing a league-low 179.8 passing yards per game in 2022.

Wilson earned plenty of respect in Philadelphia, including from cornerback Darius Slay, who spoke highly of his coaching and viewed him as a potential defensive coordinator in waiting. However, Wilson was passed over for Philadelphia's defensive coordinator opening in 2023 when the Eagles ultimately chose Sean Desai.

Wilson later left for the Baltimore Ravens, joining John Harbaugh's staff as defensive backs coach. Two seasons as the Tennessee Titans' defensive coordinator followed (2024-2025) before Wilson reunited with Harbaugh in New York in 2026. Now he's on the other sideline, responsible for designing a defensive plan against the organization that passed him over for a promotion.

That history adds another layer to Sunday's matchup. Wilson knows the Eagles' personnel and has firsthand experience coaching several players who remain in Philadelphia. His familiarity with the organization could help as he prepares the Giants' defense, and the Eagles will have to contend with a coordinator who knows how they operate.

The Eagles and Giants don't need much help making this rivalry interesting, but these stories remind us how much history and familiarity exist between the organizations. Some connections stretch back decades, while others involve people who have crossed paths on both sidelines. Milton and McCarthy's unexpected Michigan connection is another reminder of how quickly football careers can intersect in surprising ways.

Of course, none of that will matter once Sunday's game begins. The players will have their own business to handle, and the coaches will be focused on finding an edge. Still, for fans who enjoy the details beyond the final score, this matchup offers plenty of reasons to pay attention beyond who leaves Philadelphia with a victory.

articles.title: New WWE Rumors on Creed Brothers' Status After Being Moved to Company's Alumni Section
articles.summary: Former NXT tag team champions the Creed Brothers are reportedly departing WWE after six years with the company.
articles.body:
Former NXT tag team champions the Creed Brothers are reportedly departing WWE after six years with the company.

According to Fightful's Sean Ross Sapp , Julius and Brutus Creed saw their WWE contracts expire, and their WWE exit "appears to be a mutual parting of ways."

Sapp's report came on the heels of multiple social media posts by people who noticed the Creed Brothers had been moved from the active roster to the alumni section on WWE.com:

What Cruz Montana Debut Says About NXT 🤔

Julius and Brutus signed developmental deals with WWE in late 2020 and early 2021, respectively, and by the summer of 2021, they were a consistent presence on NXT programming.

The Creeds won the 2022 Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic and then won the NXT Tag Team Championships later that year.

They got called up to WWE's main roster in 2023 and joined forces with Chad Gable the following year, but they never quite found their footing as a tag team on Raw or SmackDown.

Julius and Brutus had recently returned to NXT in September and competed in the 2026 Dusty Rhodes Tag Team Classic.

Their final WWE match was a loss to Hank & Tank in the quarterfinals of the tournament on Oct. 20.

Given their ability and background, the Creed Brothers figure to generate at least some interest from other pro wrestling companies as free agents.

Julius, whose real name is Jacob Kasper, was an ACC heavyweight amateur wrestling champion at Duke University, while Brutus, whose real name is Drew Kasper, was a two-time Division III All-American in wrestling.

Pro wrestling promotions often look for that type of legitimacy in their wrestlers, which suggests that the Creed Brothers could be an option for AEW, TNA, New Japan Pro-Wrestling, MLW and any number of other companies outside of WWE.

articles.summary: La selección española supera a Portugal por 2-0, aunque necesita remontar en el primer partido, y se cita con Argentina en la final
articles.body: España cumplió con los pronósticos y estará en la final del Mundial de pádel de Doha 2026. La selección española derrotó a Portugal por 2-0, aunque tuvo que trabajar más de lo previsto para cerrar su clasificación. Una remontada necesaria para encarrilar la eliminatoria. Con el marcador a favor, Paquito Navarro y Juan Lebrón asumieron la responsabilidad de cerrar el pase. Después, Agustín Tapia y Fede Chingotto sellaron el segundo punto frente a Aris Patiniotis y Michele Brambilla por 6-3 y 6-2. Las dos grandes favoritas se verán las caras por el título. España y Argentina, frente a frente, en la final que todos esperaban. articles.body:
With the Florida State football program firing head coach Mike Norvell, speculation has been swirling in the sports world about who should replace him and lead the Seminoles in the foreseeable future. As Jimbo Fisher has been a popular name linked to the Florida State football team, the former head coach would reflect on leaving Tallahassee, Florida, back in 2017.

Speaking on the "Trials to Triumph" podcast, Fisher would speak about his time as head coach with the Seminoles from 2010 to 2017, and how leaving was the "most difficult thing I've ever done," further saying that he "never wanted to go."

"We had great success," Fisher said, via Josh Chambers. "The last couple years we didn't, but that run we had there, I did not ever want to leave. I don't want to get into this the wrong way. I just knew, kind of, the situation the ACC is in now. I saw those things and tried to get us ahead of that a little bit."

"I wanted more stuff for our staff and players, and some more facilities, because I knew where the game was going and where we were putting our money," Fisher continued. "It just never worked out. I'm not going to throw anybody under the bus. Sometimes you have to do it."

Jimbo Fisher continues on painful Florida State football exit

Fisher's name has come up in connection with the Florida State football team now that Norvell has been fired, as no one can tell if the program would be interested in a reunion. If there's one thing for certain, Fisher loves the school.

"But listen, I grew up a Florida State fan; I love Florida State, I grew up loving Florida State," Fisher said. "The Bowdens were like family to me, and I was like family to them. It was one of the most difficult things I've ever done…I remember I cried. You remember me? I cried. It killed me. But life takes turns sometimes."

It remains to be seen who the Seminoles get as their next head coach and if Fisher would be considered.

articles.title: Arizona Cardinals GM explains Jacoby Brissett, Marvin Harrison Jr. trades
articles.summary: The Arizona Cardinals have made two notable trades in the past month. Could more be coming ahead of the trade deadline?
articles.body:
It's been a busy month for Arizona Cardinals general manager Monti Ossenfort.

First came the organization's decision to trade Marvin Harrison Jr. to the Houston Texans , back on Oct. 11. Then, four weeks later, Ossenfort sent quarterback Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens , parting ways with the player who had started 20 consecutive games for Arizona.

Holding his first press conference since those moves, Ossenfort described the Brissett trade as "a little bit of a perfect storm of a lot of things."

One of those elements was the draft compensation. Ossenfort confirmed that Arizona is sending Brissett and its 2027 fifth-round pick to Baltimore, in exchange for the Ravens' 2027 fourth-round pick and 2028 seventh-round pick.

While the fourth-round pick is the key piece of draft capital, the balance of the overall compensation is equivalent to a late fifth or early sixth-round pick. That is the typical trade value for a journeyman quarterback of Brissett's caliber.

See photos of Jacoby Brissett's time with the Arizona Cardinals

The Ravens did not previously have their own pick in the fifth or sixth round, necessitating the creative package for Brissett, which came together after they lost both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injury.

"Baltimore was dealing with their own set of injury issues that happened with them on Sunday," Ossenfort said. "So then discussions started there. And then continued over the next couple of days."

At the same time, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur decided to start Gardner Minshew and demote Brissett to third-string quarterback . That effectively ended Brissett's tenure in Arizona, even before the trade.

"As the team is built, Jacoby's in that third role and an opportunity came to trade him for some value," Ossenfort said.

The other element at play is the development of third-round rookie quarterback Carson Beck. Beck is now the Cardinals' backup quarterback, meaning he will get full reps with the scout team in practice. Previously, he and Minshew had been splitting those opportunities.

"Part of this is it allows us to continue Carson's development," Ossenfort said. "And I think when you have a quarterback situation the way it was constituted here for the first couple months of the season, it's hard to always find reps and development. There's only so much practice time to go around."

Both Ossenfort and LaFleur declined to commit to Beck starting games this season, although LaFleur has previously acknowledged that "it'd be nice to know what we've got right there" when asked about Beck.

"The practice reps is first and foremost," LaFleur said. "He'll be able to rack that up. But not paving a way for anything."

Ossenfort explains Marvin Harrison Jr. trade

As with the Brissett trade, the Cardinals' decision to deal Harrison only crystallized when "an opportunity presented itself," in Ossenfort's words.

In that case, the opportunity was a second-round pick, which is currently slated to be near the top of that round, as the Texans sit at 2-5.

But it was also, Ossenfort acknowledged, a product of how Harrison's role had changed over the past year. Prior to the trade, he had just five catches on 13 targets, as he fell behind Trey McBride and Michael Wilson in the Cardinals' offensive pecking order.

"Marv's role evolved into what it was for us," Ossenfort said. "And so, at that point, we had to decide: should we go forward and is it gonna come out of that role, is it gonna be different? Or … we're getting offered something that we think is pretty valuable here, do we pivot and take that? And that's the decision that we made."

Harrison, the No. 4 overall pick in 2024, finished his Cardinals career with just 1,578 receiving yards in 33 games.

Ossenfort broadly pushed back on the notion that the Cardinals missed with their draft pick of Harrison.

"Sometimes those expectations that are put on players are unfair," Ossenfort said.

Marvin Harrison Jr.'s Arizona Cardinals career at a glance

Still, he acknowledged that it was not the ending the organization envisioned for Harrison's career in Arizona.

"A lot goes into that," Ossenfort said. "It really is never about one thing. … A lot of reasons why it didn't work out. Probably can't get into all of them. But I will definitely say it wasn't for lack of effort from anybody's part. I think the world of who Marvin is as a person."

With the NFL trade deadline looming on Nov. 10, Ossenfort left open the possibility for more trades.

"I don't really know," Ossenfort said. "We'll see how that works out."

In explaining the uncertainty regarding any potential moves, Ossenfort pointed to the progression of the Cardinals' previous two trades.

"Everybody says, well, this guy's being shopped," Ossenfort said. "A lot of times that's just not accurate. It really comes down to — as in these cases of the trades that we just made — is someone going to get aggressive and try to make it happen? And otherwise, it's a lot of talk and a lot of, 'Hey, maybe, maybe not.'"

In the case of Harrison, the Cardinals reportedly held discussions with other teams for two weeks leading up to the trade, but a deal only got across the finish line once a second-round pick was on the table. And in the case of Brissett, the Ravens' injury situation necessitated immediate action.

So far, that sense of urgency has not yet arrived with any of the Cardinals' other potential trade candidates, including edge rusher Josh Sweat and safety Budda Baker.

"Let's see how things get serious," Ossenfort said. "And obviously deadlines have a way of making people get serious."

articles.title: Giants-Eagles final injury report: Cam Skattebo misses practice, doubtful for Sunday
articles.summary: Odds are Skattebo won’t play vs. Eagles.
articles.body:
Cam Skattebo missed a fourth straight practice on Friday due to his hamstring injury, but the New York Giants are not ruling their leading rusher out for Sunday's game against the Philadelphia Eagles. Skattebo is officially considered doubtful.

"Let's see what happens" head coach John Harbaugh said of Skattebo's status.

Wide receiver Malik Nabers , who missed practice on Thursday, yelled to reporters that he practice on Friday . Harbaugh said that Nabers' health is "not an issue" for Sunday.

If Skattebo cannot play, Devin Singletary will be the Giants' primary running back against the Eagles. Gregory Desrosiers is the other back on the 53-man roster, and Phil Mafah and Eric Gray are on the practice squad.

The other injury of note for the Giants involves wide reciever/returner Charlie Jones . He turned up on the injury report this week with a hand injury, and is listed as questionable.

"He's managing it," Harbaugh said. "He was out today catching and everything like that. Just want to make sure he could catch. I haven't talked to him yet. We'll see how he felt."

The Giants have an open roster spot after dropping quarterback Jake Haener from the 53-man roster on Thursday. Adding someone with running back, return experience, or both, might make sense before Sunday.

Running back Saquon Barkley (hamstring/back) was limited in practice on Friday, but does have an injury designation. That means he will play on Sunday.

articles.title: Tourney talk: Northwestern football’s path to the College Football Playoff
articles.summary: There’s potential, but it’s gonna take perfection, plus a lot of help.
articles.body:
The College Football Playoff Committee released their first top-25 rankings just three days ago, and as controversial as this was, there are two monumental takeaways.

The SEC is held in as high of a regard as it was in the Nick Saban era, even after all the turbulence within the conference.

Besides Indiana and UCLA, the committee doesn't believe in the Big Ten this season.

The latter of those statements includes Northwestern, who despite being ranked No. 23 by the AFCA Coaches Poll, was dropped from the top-25 by the AP and the CFP after a one-touchdown loss to Oregon, who snuck in at No. 23 in the CFP rankings. That means it's time for us to regroup and re-evaluate NU's chances at making the tournament.

With four weeks of the regular season left, time is of the essence for NU. Its playoff hopes are dwindling, but haven't faded yet. There's a still a small chance, but it's going to take some elbow grease and a whole lot of luck.

The good: Why NU was considered a CFP contender

The buzz for Northwestern started after it took then-No. 5 Indiana to the brink of defeat, even after the slowest first half of offense it played this year. It started to show its clutch factor — scoring 16 points in the fourth quarter, the most an opponent had posted against IU in the Curt Cignetti era — and if it wasn't for one fatal face mask penalty, that game could've went the other way. A win, and Northwestern would've immediately jumped into the polls. Instead, it got a singular vote from Greg Luca of the San Antonio Express.

That wasn't just pity. It was intentional, based on the tape produced by the Wildcats' offense.

In terms of system fit, Northwestern's personnel is up there with any team in the country: a dual-threat quarterback in Aidan Chiles, two gritty yardage-eaters in the backfield alongside him in Caleb Komolafe and Gavin Sawchuk, a prototypical deep-ball threat in Griffin Wilde, a sneaky-athletic slot receiver in Drew Wagner, freakishly athletic tight ends in Luke Dehnicke and Alex Honig, and the Swiss army knife, Joseph Himon II. Put all of that together, and you've got an innovative wing-T offense that shifts, motions and counters to no end.

It's an offense that the majority of NU's opponents haven't been able to figure out.

Not South Dakota State, who couldn't contain Chiles or stop the jet sweep in Week 1.

Not Colorado, who couldn't I.D. Himon out of the backfield in Week 3.

And for a time in the second half, not even IU, who kept losing Wilde and Dehnicke over the middle in Week 4.

This offense is what dominated in back-to-back weeks, posting nearly flawless showings that flashed the best of both worlds: the ground game against Penn State, the pass game against Ball State.

Pair that with the second-best red zone defense in the Big Ten, that allows scores just 75% of the time, and that's a top-25 team.

By Week 8, NU had checked off every box it could, thrashing the opponents it was expected to beat and snagging a gritty road win in an emotional reunion with former head coach Pat Fitzgerald inside Spartan Stadium.

Then, it went to Eugene, and some chinks in the armor were exposed.

The bad: Why NU is on the outside looking in

There's a lot to unpack that we at Inside NU haven't gotten around to after the 'Cats first-ever trip to Eugene, so let's do that.

Firstly, before anything, it's important to note Northwestern's luck, for better or for worse. Before the start of the season, Halloween was supposed to be the start of an extended spooky season for the Wildcats, facing the preseason No. 2, No. 22 and No. 1 in succession. Two of those teams — Oregon and Ohio State — have dropped in the polls, losing their starting quarterbacks in the process. The third, Iowa, is going through quarterback turbulence right now and doesn't even have a starter named on the depth chart for Week 10.

Before the start of the year, CBS analyst Brad Crawford ranked NU's schedule as the hardest in all of college football, quite literally saying "they aren't making the playoff this season" in a conversation with Claudia Bellofatto.

But he had a point. Oregon and Ohio State's only losses in 2025 were to the eventual national champ Indiana. In the year before, the Ducks won the Big Ten Championship over Penn State, while OSU won the natty in a stretch of four uncompetitive games. Iowa was the model of consistency during those two seasons as well, going 8-5 in '24 and 9-4 in '25.

The Hawkeyes, right now, are arguably the best team of the trio. Oregon lost both its coordinators — OC Will Stein to Kentucky (what a gamble for the Wildcats, huh?) and DC Tosh Lupoi to Cal. Drew Mehringer was given the keys to the offense, and couldn't do the job, getting the booth after a 21-10 loss to Illinois in Week 8. Ohio State was gunning for the nation's No. 1 spot until Julian Sayin suffered an arm injury against Indiana in Week 8. Luke Fahey stepped in his place and was given the wake-up call of his young career against USC.

On top of all this, the Iowa State import into Happy Valley didn't make Penn State nearly as good as it was hyped to be, while Colorado and Michigan State just can't figure it out this year. NU has scooped up more definitive wins as a result, but its strength of schedule (SOS) has suffered.

When you look at who's in and who's out of the first edition of the CFP poll, SOS matters a lot. A 5-3 Florida team playing .500 SEC football can get in with the No. 3 strength of schedule in the nation, per ESPN. It's losses? No. 25 Mizzou, No. 3 Georgia and now-No. 21 South Carolina.

Wait, what? Why are the 5-3 Gamecocks here?

They are 15th in SOS in the country. On top of that, they have a win over No. 11 Tennessee and a TIGHT loss to then-No. 24, now No. 6, Kentucky.

Northwestern, right now, is 34th in that metric. So it doesn't matter how well it plays. If it's not seen as quality competition, it doesn't move the needle.

Oregon, being 21st in SOS, was the first true test for the Wildcats. They failed.

But there are chances for redemption on the horizon.

The roadmap: Who needs to heat up and cool down?

10 SEC teams are in the CFP top 25. That doesn't bode well for a non-blue blood Power Four team like NU, who doesn't get the "benefit of the doubt." Some teams need to tumble, but others need to rattle off some wins to boost the Wildcats' resume.

Northwestern . Self explanatory. In the past two years, three-loss teams have only made the CFP if they've been in the SEC and their third loss was in the conference title game (looking at you, 'Bama). NU's already got two losses. It has no more lifelines. The 'Cats can't afford another loss in the regular season. MAYBE if every domino falls their way and they get to the Big Ten Championship, we can talk about what a "good loss" might do to solidify their chances of getting into the playoff. For now, it's do-or-die.

Oregon . Also self-explanatory. U of O doesn't have the hardest of schedules to end the year, taking on a Sayin-less No. 12 Ohio State this week before rounding out the year with Michigan, Michigan State and Washington. Not the cream of the crop, but if the Ducks end with a 8-4 record, a loss at Autzen Stadium gains so much more credibility.

Here's the catch. They need to lose one of those games. Why? Because NU needs to heighten its chances to get into the Big Ten Championship as much as possible. The safest bet here, without dropping out of the polls, would be to back Michigan State, who gave Northwestern a dogfight and put up a fight against Notre Dame earlier in the year.

Illinois. Okay, yes, I know what you're thinking. Why would I EVER root for Illinois as a Northwestern fan? Hear me out for two seconds.

I'm not saying the Illini should run the table. In fact, the best case scenario would be for them to finish the year 1-3. What I am advocating for is for competitiveness. Keep it tight with UCLA and Iowa, force them out of their offenses, make these games low-scoring affairs and test their guts. It makes the prospect of a multi-touchdown win for Northwestern on rivalry week more enticing for the CFP committee to look at in relation to the other ranked Big Ten teams.

Miami. Right now the ACC has two teams in the hunt to secure an at-large bid for the CFP: No. 1 Miami (8-0) and No. 16 Wake Forest (7-1). However, 6-2 teams SMU, Virginia Tech and Duke are also all still in the hunt to make the ACC title game, and with a big win over Miami in that game, they could steal a bid and vault themselves into the field of 12, shrinking the at-large field to 10 teams. That would be catastrophic for Northwestern.

So if you're a 'Cats fan, the ACC needs to blow up. It's okay if Miami wins the conference — in fact, this is what NU wants to happen.

However, outside of the Hurricanes, NU can't afford for another ACC team to make it into the field. Wake Forest needs to pick up a loss against SMU or Duke, while SMU needs to fall to Notre Dame and Duke must lose to Miami.

And, most importantly, Miami needs to win the ACC title game, so that the conference doesn't produce a bid stealer.

Indiana . The biggest threat to NU's conference title hopes with the head-to-head win at home. Asking the Hoosiers to lose to USC seems reasonable. Asking them to lose to Washington or Purdue is a difficult ask. But it needs to happen. Three losses for the Hoosiers and Northwestern is right back in the mix.

UCLA . To be honest, it's way more likely that NU sneaks into the Big Ten title game if the Bruins lose twice within the next four weeks. Minnesota on the road is a tall task, and USC at the Rose Bowl is bound to bring out Rivalry Week emotion. Those are the two games I've got UCLA on upset alert for.

Notre Dame. NU's odds at sneaking in as a 10 or 11 seed increase exponentially if the Fighting Irish lose to Miami AND a team like SMU or Syracuse. It's certainly possible. North Carolina made it competitive when they went on the road to Chapel Hill and BYU made a case for being the nation's best team by besting them in Provo. Can 'Cuse get it done in The Dome? I'd give it a shot after the Orange won last Saturday against the Mustangs.

Georgia. The more the SEC crumbles, the better. There's been so much parity in the conference in 2026: first, everyone thought Texas was the team to beat. Then, Auburn became the story of the conference. Then, Kentucky blew everyone's minds with a pair of overtime wins over South Carolina and LSU. But through it all, the Bulldogs have been consistently good-to-great. One slip, though, and smoke and mirrors cloud everyone's perception of the SEC.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 9 Start 'Em Sit 'Em: Denzel Boston or Ladd McConkey?
articles.summary: Which wide receiver has a better outlook in Week 9 fantasy football: Denzel Boston or Ladd McConkey?
articles.body:
Today's fantasy focus is on the wide receiver position. Denzel Boston has been a key part of his overperforming Browns offense, while Ladd McConkey is on an underperforming Chargers offense. Who is the better player in Week 9 fantasy football? Let's find out.

Boston has a 93% route rate this season, with an 18.4% target-per-route run rate. Recency bias matters, especially at wide receiver. In Boston's last three games, he has had a 93% route rate and a 22.3% target-per-route run rate.

The Browns are quite healthy in Week 9, so there's virtually no variance there at Boston's WR1 spot.

How good really is Boston? Here are some of his advanced metrics:

In the red zone, Boston has a 28% target share. That is 29% inside the 10-yard line. Boston has zero red-zone touchdowns, but I would venture to say the law of averages will start working in its favor, resulting in a red-zone touchdown in any game now.

The Browns have a 57% red zone pass rate, about NFL average.

As for Boston's Week 9 matchup, he faces the New Orleans Saints. They rank 13th-best in Yards per Target Allowed to outside wide receivers and 23rd in EPA per Pass Allowed.

The Browns do start Shedeur Sanders this week. Luckily for him, the Saints rank 28th in Pressure Rate , which offsets the Browns' 30th-place ranking in Pressure Rate Allowed. Matchup: Average

McConkey's usage rates are skewed this season due to lingering health issues. The good news is that he appears fully healthy for Week 9. To analyze his usage rates, we will focus on two games where he was mostly healthy: Weeks 3 and 8.

When healthy, McConkey has a 86% route rate and 15% Target per Route Run Rate.

The Chargers are healthy this week, so there is no skewing of McConkey's potential usage.

It's honestly deceptive to look at McConkey's advanced metrics, since many of them reflect games he played while unhealthy. What we do know is that, at his best, McConkey is probably a top-20 wide receiver in the NFL. He needs Justin Herbert to help him play better football.

What I can analyze is McConkey's Yards per Reception and Average Depth of Target. They are 16.8 yards and 13.1 yards, respectively, which are very strong.

This season, McConkey has only two red-zone targets. For reference, McConkey has run 128 total routes this season. So, less than 2% of McConkey's targets have come in that golden area.

McConkey competes against the Houston Texans this week. The Texans rank just 25th in Yards per Target Allowed to wide receivers. McConkey lines up in the slot and out wide, which the Texans are quite bad against in both alignments.

In EPA per Pass Allowed, the Texans rank 22nd. They also rank 20th in Pressure Rate, and the Chargers rank 31st in Pressure Rate Allowed. Justin Herbert is 27th in EPA per Dropback vs. Blitz. Matchup: Average.

Start 'Em Sit 'Em: Denzel Boston vs. Ladd McConkey

Boston will be the play this week. He has more consistent, proven volume within his offense. While Shedeur Sanders will start, I still gauge McConkey as the player with more variance risk, having spent so much time this season hurt and on a bad offense.
